Riaz Mohammad Khan (Foreign Secretary of Pakistan)
Sima Samar (Head of the Afghan Independent Human Rights Commission)
Rangin Dâdfar Spantâ (Minister for Foreign Affairs)
Tom Koenigs (Special Representative of the Secretary-General)

records.record_text: The Security Council mission to Afghanistan was its second since 2003 in support of the Afghan people (see S/2003/1074). It found that the Afghan partnership, begun in Bonn, Germany, in late 2001, was largely on track.

The successful establishment of functioning democratic institutions and efforts to improve the welfare of the population since 2001 now required consolidation to ensure that Afghanistan embarked on a period of genuine stability and development.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the need to move from institution-building to consolidation and delivery of results.

records.record_text: Nevertheless, progress in 2006 towards realizing the vision of the Afghanistan Compact has not been as rapid as had been hoped.
records.policy_implication: Indicates a gap between expectations and reality in the implementation of the Compact.

records.record_text: The past year has been characterized by uneven efforts to improve governance and establish the rule of law, intensification of the Taliban-led insurgency, an upsurge in illegal drug production and trafficking, widespread insecurity in the south and east of the country and continued impunity for criminals, corrupt officials and commanders of illegal armed groups.
records.policy_implication: Establishes the nexus of insecurity, poor governance, and criminality as the core challenge.

records.record_text: These factors — countered only partially by fragile State institutions — have tempered the legitimate hopes of Afghans with signs of despondency and disillusionment. The mission noted that the confidence of the Afghan public in its new institutions and processes was being tested.
records.policy_implication: Warns of the political consequences of failing to address security and governance deficits, specifically the erosion of public trust.

records.record_text: Faced with these realities, the mission stressed two cardinal messages: firstly, that the firm and unyielding commitment of the international community in support of the Government and people of Afghanistan and their country’s transition was unwavering; and secondly, the Afghanistan Compact, owned and led by Afghans, remains the central, strategic framework for cooperation between the Government of Afghanistan and the international community.
records.political_signal: Unwavering international commitment and centrality of the Afghanistan Compact.
records.policy_implication: Aimed to counter narratives of international fatigue and reinforce the agreed political framework.

records.record_text: Security was the dominant concern in Afghanistan.

The insurgency appeared more or less confined to one third of the country. The remaining two thirds of Afghanistan (west, north and central regions) were considered comparatively stable. However, limited factional tensions were emerging in the north and trends towards rearmament had been detected.
records.policy_implication: While the insurgency is geographically contained, risks of instability are present even in 'stable' areas.

records.record_text: ISAF Commander General David J. Richards noted that Operation Medusa in Kandahar Province in September 2006 had dealt the Taliban-led insurgency a heavy blow. He predicted that this and other recent operations by Afghan and international military forces had set the stage for a more stable winter and 2007.
records.policy_implication: Presents an optimistic military assessment of recent operations.

records.record_text: On the last point, however, more cautious views were expressed by UNAMA, the United Nations country team and civil society members. In any case, if there are medium-term gains, they would be dependent on the swift delivery of reconstruction, development and improved governance in insurgent-affected areas.
records.policy_implication: Military gains are fragile and must be followed by immediate governance and development action to be sustainable.

records.record_text: The Afghan leadership observed that the growth of the insurgency had been fed by the failure of the Government of Afghanistan and the international community to provide basic services, governance and security to rural communities.
records.policy_implication: An admission of state failure as a root cause of the insurgency.

records.record_text: A number of interlocutors highlighted the weakness of the Afghan National Police and the rule of law as major factors contributing to the rise in instability.
The National Security Adviser, Zalmai Rassoul, said that the narcotics industry was the number one problem for national security.
records.policy_implication: Elevates counter-narcotics to the highest level of national security concern.

records.record_text: The mission took note of the Afghan view that the insurgency in Afghanistan cannot be brought to a halt with the existence of sanctuaries for insurgents in neighbouring countries.
records.political_signal: Afghan leadership's assertion that the solution to the insurgency lies partly outside Afghanistan's borders.

records.record_text: Minister for Foreign Affairs Rangin Dâdfar Spantâ underscored the importance of providing a clear, unmistakable message to the population that the international community would stay the course in Afghanistan, as rumours to the contrary fuelled insecurity.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the political and security impact of perceptions of international commitment.

records.record_text: UNAMA noted that the list established pursuant to Security Council resolution 1267 (1999) contained some inaccuracies and observed that an updated list would be an important tool in the international fight against terrorism and for stability in the region.
records.policy_implication: A request to the Security Council to improve the effectiveness of its own sanctions regime as a tool for stability in Afghanistan.

records.record_text: The mission paid tribute to the leading role that ISAF, led by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), had assumed in contributing to security in support of the Government of Afghanistan.
records.political_signal: Acknowledgement and endorsement of ISAF's role and sacrifices.

records.record_text: The mission took note of the continuing need of ISAF for adequate forces and resources to ensure the continued success of the ISAF operations.
records.policy_implication: Signals a potential resource gap for the international military mission.

records.record_text: The Deputy Speaker of the Meshrano Jirga, Sayed Hamed Gailani, said that international security forces would need to respect the culture and religion of Afghanistan in order to retain the support of the population.
records.policy_implication: Links the tactical behavior of international forces to strategic popular support.

records.record_text: Afghan ministers and parliamentarians called for better coordination and increased information sharing between international security forces and the Government of Afghanistan.
records.policy_implication: A request for greater partnership and respect for Afghan sovereignty in security operations.

records.record_text: President Karzai and other Afghan interlocutors expressed frustration with the state of the Afghan National Police. The President faulted Afghanistan’s international partners for inadequate and belated efforts to develop the Afghan National Police, a failure which he claimed was partly to blame for the insecurity on the Afghanistan-Pakistan border.
records.political_signal: Attributing partial blame for insecurity to the international community's failure on police reform.

records.record_text: Throughout the mission, interlocutors cited corruption and the perpetuation of a culture of impunity as the root causes of popular Afghan disaffection and unease.
records.policy_implication: Identifies anti-corruption and ending impunity as central to winning public support.

records.record_text: Sima Samar, the head of the Afghan Independent Human Rights Commission, and others pointed to widespread corruption in law enforcement and judicial institutions as central to the population’s decreasing trust in the Government.
It was also pointed out that the continued tolerance of positions of authority given to the former commanders and warlords was contributing to instability.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the direct link between impunity for powerful figures and ongoing instability.

records.record_text: President Karzai identified restructuring the civil service and strengthening its capacity as the top priority for Afghanistan and its international partners.
records.political_signal: Establishes public sector reform as the President's number one priority.

records.record_text: During the mission’s meeting with the Joint Coordination and Monitoring Board and later with Afghan development ministers, interlocutors observed that “parallel administrations” had emerged — one international and one Afghan.
records.policy_implication: Identifies a key structural problem in aid delivery that undermines Afghan state-building.

records.record_text: The United Nations country team stated that following the ousting of the Taliban in 2001 space had opened for human rights and gender equality... However, the country team was concerned that this space had recently begun to close.
records.policy_implication: Signals a reversal of post-2001 gains in human and women's rights.

records.record_text: The mission noted with concern suggestions that the Ministry of Women’s Affairs might be abolished.
records.policy_implication: Highlights a significant threat to the institutional framework for women's rights in Afghanistan.

records.record_text: Afghanistan’s burgeoning narco-economy was identified by the vast majority of the mission’s interlocutors as a primary threat to stability.

President Karzai characterized the spectacular growth of poppy cultivation as a sign of desperation in the Afghan people, which would only be remedied through stronger governance as well as reconstruction and economic development.
records.policy_implication: Frames the narcotics problem as a symptom of under-development and poor governance, not just a criminal issue.

records.record_text: Over the past few months, ISAF had detected a 70 per cent and 50 per cent increase, respectively, in security incidents in the Afghan provinces of Paktika and Khost, which neighbour North Waziristan.
records.policy_implication: Provides specific data linking a peace deal in Pakistan to increased violence in Afghanistan.

records.record_text: The mission encouraged Pakistan to monitor the North Waziristan agreement with a view to ensuring that the cross-border impact of this or any future agreements are positive for security and stability.
records.policy_implication: A diplomatic request for Pakistan to take responsibility for the cross-border consequences of its internal policies.

records.record_text: The mission expressed concern regarding the humanitarian implications of possible contingencies to employ, even if selectively, landmines along the border to control cross-border movement.
records.political_signal: A clear signal of disapproval for the potential use of landmines.

records.record_text: The mission found that the spread of insurgency, and terrorist activity by the Taliban, Al-Qaida and other extremist groups, linked with the illegal drug trade, coupled with corruption and failures of governance and the rule of law, collectively pose a grave threat to reconstruction and nation-building in Afghanistan.
records.policy_implication: The mission's main overarching finding, defining the interconnected nature of the threats to Afghanistan.

records.record_text: The Security Council will undertake to ensure that the international community’s support for Afghanistan and its commitment to this shared strategy remain firm and enduring.
records.political_signal: A formal commitment from the Security Council itself to maintain international support.

records.record_text: The mission reaffirms its support for the Afghanistan Compact as the best framework for cooperation between the Government of Afghanistan and the international community.
records.political_signal: Endorsement of the Afghanistan Compact as the sole strategic framework.

records.record_text: The mission urges NATO and other countries to maintain and, where possible, increase their commitment to ISAF to meet the challenge of the current security environment in Afghanistan.
records.policy_implication: A direct call for more troops and resources for the international military effort.

records.record_text: The mission affirms the importance of establishing a strong and sustainable Afghan National Army and urges donors and the Government of Afghanistan to redouble their collective efforts to establish a trusted and effective Afghan National Police throughout the country.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the critical failure in police development and calls for a major course correction.

records.record_text: As a matter of highest priority, the mission urges the Government of Afghanistan with the support of its international partners to establish rule of law and good governance throughout the country.
records.policy_implication: Elevates rule of law and good governance to the 'highest priority'.

records.record_text: The mission encourages the Government to take immediate steps to strengthen justice sector institutions and provincial government, including through the replacement of corrupt officials and local power brokers.
records.policy_implication: A specific and politically sensitive recommendation to remove corrupt officials, tackling impunity head-on.

records.record_text: The mission urges the Government and donors to make the empowerment of women a true cross-cutting priority and to actively defend the provisions for the rights of women that are enshrined in the Constitution of Afghanistan.
records.policy_implication: Response to the observed rollback of women's rights.

records.record_text: The mission urges both Governments [Afghanistan and Pakistan] to increase dialogue and collaboration in the face of a growing threat to their shared security.

The mission recommends that the list established pursuant to Security Council resolution 1267 (1999) continue to be updated as necessary and on the basis of the most up-to-date information, as envisaged by the relevant Security Council resolutions.
records.policy_implication: A recommendation for the Council's own sanctions committee to act on information received during the mission.

records.record_text: The mission reaffirms the central and impartial role of the United Nations in promoting peace and stability in Afghanistan.
records.political_signal: Endorsement of the UN's lead role in coordinating the international effort.

records.record_text: The mission calls upon the international community to revitalize its support to the increased efforts of the Government of Afghanistan to implement the programme to disband illegally armed groups.
records.policy_implication: Signals that the DIAG programme has stalled and requires renewed political and financial backing.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Sudan and Chad, 4-10 June 2006

main_risks: Failure of the Darfur Peace Agreement due to non-signatories and implementation delays.
Collapse of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement due to unresolved issues (Abyei), lack of a peace dividend, and insecurity in the south.
Escalation of regional conflict between Sudan and Chad.
Severe deterioration of the humanitarian and security situation in Darfur and eastern Chad.
The ongoing threat posed by the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA).
main_commitments: To pursue a seven-stage process for the transition from AMIS to a UN operation in Darfur.
To review the issue of international protection for refugee and IDP camps in Chad and request recommendations from the Secretary-General.
To remain in regular dialogue with the Government of the Sudan regarding the UN force deployment.
To consider the AU's request to reconsider the arms embargo on Somalia if an IGAD peacekeeping operation is mounted.
main_policy_signals: A UN peacekeeping operation in Darfur with a robust Chapter VII mandate is necessary, despite the Government of Sudan's objections.
The international community respects Sudan's sovereignty but will not accept inaction on civilian protection in Darfur.
The Government of Sudan holds the primary responsibility for implementing the Darfur Peace Agreement, especially the disarmament of the Janjaweed.
Parties obstructing the Darfur Peace Agreement may face sanctions.
The Sudan-Chad conflict requires dialogue and implementation of the Tripoli Agreement.
LRA leaders indicted by the ICC must be brought to justice.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: This was a high-level diplomatic mission conducted in a complex and volatile period following the signing of the Darfur Peace Agreement (DPA). The mission's primary objective was to secure the Government of Sudan's consent for a UN peacekeeping force in Darfur, which was met with firm rejection by President Al-Bashir. The mission observed significant challenges to both the DPA and the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (CPA), a dire humanitarian situation, and severe regional tensions between Sudan and Chad. Key findings included deep divisions on the proposed UN force, with the government and allied tribal leaders opposing it while IDPs, refugees, and the SPLM were supportive. The report concludes with a detailed roadmap for a phased transition to a UN force in Darfur, strong recommendations for CPA implementation, and calls for de-escalation between Sudan and Chad.

activities.activity_description: Met with President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, Minister for Foreign Affairs Lam Akol, SPLM Cabinet Affairs Minister Deng Alor, members of the National Assembly, representatives of the Sudanese opposition parties and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in Khartoum.
Received briefing from the leadership of the United Nations Mission in the Sudan (UNMIS) in Khartoum.

Met with First Vice-President Salva Kiir, senior officials of the Government of Southern Sudan, the Ceasefire Joint Military Committee, members of the Southern Sudan Legislative Assembly, members of the United Nations country team and NGOs in Juba.

Met with Force Commander Major General Ihekire and the wider leadership of the African Union Mission in Sudan (AMIS), the Wali of Northern Darfur, internally displaced persons (IDPs), NGOs, representatives of civil society, tribal leaders, diplomatic representatives and members of the United Nations country team in El Fasher (Darfur).
Visited Khartoum, Juba and El Fasher in the Sudan.
Visited the African Union (AU) headquarters in Addis Ababa.
Visited N’djamena and Goz Beida in Chad.

Met with Chairperson Alpha Oumar Konaré and other members of the AU Commission (including Commissioner for Peace and Security Said Djinnit), the Peace and Security Council and AMIS troop-contributing countries in Addis Ababa.
Met with President Idriss Déby and his cabinet, diplomatic representatives and members of the United Nations country team in Chad.
Met with Sudanese refugees and Chadian internally displaced persons in Goz Beida, Chad.
Briefly met with Under-Secretary Guéhenno, who was visiting with the technical assessment mission.
Received a briefing on gender-based violence from the United Nations country team and NGOs in El Fasher.

actors_met.actor_name: United Nations Mission in the Sudan (UNMIS)

records.record_text: the Darfur conflict to be complex and not easily understood by the international community.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the need for nuanced policy approaches rather than simplistic solutions.

records.record_text: President Al-Bashir made clear to the mission that a United Nations force in Darfur with a mandate under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations was unacceptable to the Government of the Sudan.
records.political_signal: Strong rejection by the Government of Sudan of a Chapter VII UN mission, framed as a defense of sovereignty.
records.policy_implication: This is the central point of contention and the primary obstacle to the Council's preferred course of action.

records.record_text: it was for the Government of the Sudan to disarm the various militias, including the Janjaweed, by itself.
records.political_signal: Assertion of state responsibility and capacity for disarmament, rejecting external military intervention.

records.record_text: SPLM and AMIS contacts expressed their doubts that the Government of the Sudan was capable of carrying out disarmament of the militias by itself.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces the rationale for an international force by questioning the commitment and capacity of the Government of Sudan.

records.record_text: The IDPs that the mission met in the Sudan and Chad all called for United Nations protection.
records.political_signal: Direct appeal from affected populations for international intervention, contradicting the government's stance.
records.policy_implication: Adds moral and political weight to the argument for a UN protection force.

records.record_text: the mission agreed with the AU that AMIS should be urgently strengthened and a tougher mandate be adopted, including the protection of civilians, ahead of the deployment of a United Nations mission.
records.policy_implication: This is an interim solution to bridge the gap until a UN force can be deployed.

records.record_text: AMIS Force Commanders warned that, without such reinforcements, Darfur risked becoming another Rwanda.
records.political_signal: Use of 'Rwanda' is a powerful signal intended to provoke urgent international action.

records.record_text: Special Representative Pronk stressed to the mission the importance of also getting the signature of Abdul Wahid given that he appeared to have the support of a majority of the IDPs of Darfur.
records.policy_implication: The DPA's legitimacy and viability are linked to the inclusion of key rebel leaders with popular support.

records.record_text: The mission concluded that the humanitarian and security situation in Darfur remained dire and expressed concern at the deterioration of the humanitarian and security situation in camps in Chad.
The mission was encouraged by the number of key steps that had been taken on implementation of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement.
records.political_signal: Positive reinforcement for progress made on the North-South agreement.

records.record_text: interlocutors also voiced a number of challenges that were undermining implementation. These included the future status of the Abyei region, the slow speed in setting up Comprehensive Peace Agreement commissions and the lack of a peace dividend for the population owing to the failure of international donors to live up to their pledges.
records.policy_implication: These challenges pose a direct threat to the stability of the CPA.

records.record_text: the humanitarian community urged the Council not to consider cannibalizing UNMIS for any future operation in Darfur.
records.policy_implication: Creating a mission in Darfur should not come at the expense of stability in Southern Sudan.

records.record_text: the mission considered addressing the presence of Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA) a priority.
the mission advised caution in dealing politically with LRA leaders wanted for trial in The Hague.
records.political_signal: The imperative of international justice (ICC indictments) should not be sidelined for political expediency.
records.policy_implication: This reflects the tension between peace and justice, a recurring dilemma in conflict resolution.

records.record_text: Both President Al-Bashir and President Déby urged the Council to condemn the actions of the other.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates the complete breakdown of bilateral relations and attempts to leverage the Council for political gain.

records.record_text: The AU said both were acting in an underhand manner.
The mission urged dialogue between the two countries, as well as the implementation of the Tripoli Agreement.
records.actor_target: Government of Sudan; Government of Chad

records.record_text: President Al-Bashir said that the [Abyei Boundaries] Commission had failed to reach an agreement and that, as a result, he would never accept the subsequent decision of the Commission.
records.political_signal: A clear statement of non-compliance with a key provision of the CPA.
records.policy_implication: This rejection poses a fundamental threat to the CPA and future stability between North and South.

records.record_text: First Vice-President Kiir added that, if a solution was not found [for Abyei], implementation of the entire Comprehensive Peace Agreement could eventually be jeopardized.

the humanitarian community expressed concern at the growing insecurity in some areas of southern Sudan, especially Upper Nile and Jonglei, owing to the activities of militias who had not yet integrated into the Sudanese Armed Forces or SPLA.
records.actor_source: Humanitarian Community; Government of Southern Sudan
records.policy_implication: The presence of these militias is a violation of the CPA and a major source of instability.

records.record_text: The IDPs whom the Council met in El Fasher and Chad made clear their strong opposition to the Darfur Peace Agreement, as well as their demands for greater compensation.
records.policy_implication: Lack of buy-in from the affected population, particularly IDPs, is a major weakness of the DPA.

records.record_text: The mission stressed to UNMIS and AMIS the importance of explaining the benefits of the Agreement, in particular inside the camps.
records.policy_implication: Recognizes that opposition to the DPA may be based on misinformation and lack of understanding.

records.record_text: The mission emphasized that disarmament of the Janjaweed militias and other illegal armed groups was central to improving security.
records.political_signal: Disarmament of Janjaweed is a non-negotiable prerequisite for security.

records.record_text: The AU confirmed its strong support for a transfer to a United Nations operation.
records.political_signal: The AU is formally requesting the UN to take over, citing lack of resources and capacity.
records.policy_implication: Provides the legal and political basis for the Security Council to authorize a UN mission.

records.record_text: The mission assured the Government of the Sudan that any United Nations force would have strong African participation and character.
records.political_signal: An attempt to mitigate Sudanese concerns about 'colonialism' or Western intervention by emphasizing the African nature of the proposed force.

records.record_text: President Déby said that the Sudan was determined to destabilize Chad.
President Déby made a formal appeal to the Council for the United Nations to provide security for the camps against incursions by the Janjaweed and security for humanitarian workers.
records.policy_implication: This request opens the door for a potential UN security presence in Chad, expanding the scope of international engagement.

records.record_text: Humanitarian partners reported that between 60 per cent and 70 per cent of women who left the camps to collect firewood had experienced gender-based violence.
The mission strongly stressed to tribal leaders and to the Wali that it wanted to see better protection of women in Darfur, in line with Security Council resolution 1325 (2000).
records.actor_target: Tribal leaders; Wali of Northern Darfur
records.political_signal: Directly links the situation on the ground to the UNSC's broader Women, Peace and Security agenda.

records.record_text: The Council continues to give its full support to the Comprehensive Peace Agreement and the Darfur Peace Agreement, and wishes to see both implemented fully as a matter of urgency
records.political_signal: The Council views the DPA and CPA as the cornerstones of peace in Sudan and expects urgent, full implementation.

records.record_text: The Darfur Peace Agreement can provide a basis for sustained security in Darfur. Efforts should continue to get further support from non-signatories, in particular Abdul Wahid. However, implementation cannot be held up.
records.political_signal: A balanced message: inclusivity is desired, but it will not be used as an excuse for inaction by signatories.

records.record_text: The United Nations should work in partnership with the Government of the Sudan, and with its agreement, in deploying a United Nations force in Darfur.
records.political_signal: Acknowledges the principle of consent while maintaining the goal of deployment.
records.policy_implication: This frames the future UN deployment as a cooperative effort, not an imposition, despite current disagreements.

records.record_text: If the United Nations force is to make a qualitative difference and protect itself and citizens against attacks by spoilers, it will need to take over a strengthened AMIS mandate, in line with that provided for by the Darfur Peace Agreement.
records.political_signal: Signals that a weak, non-robust mandate for a UN force is not an option.
records.policy_implication: Sets the baseline for any future mandate negotiations; a 'toothless' mission will not be deployed.

records.record_text: There will be a seven-stage process towards full United Nations operational capacity in Darfur.
records.political_signal: This detailed plan signals the Council's determination and methodical approach to the transition, moving beyond rhetoric.
records.policy_implication: Establishes a concrete, sequential roadmap for the international community's actions in the coming months.

records.record_text: Given the continuing security concerns in the south, the mission considers that UNMIS should not be impacted on as a result of the deployment of a United Nations force in Darfur
records.policy_implication: This recommendation explicitly rejects 'robbing Peter to pay Paul' and underscores the need for adequate resourcing for both missions.

records.record_text: The problem of LRA requires firm attention. Steps should be taken to develop a decisive international response to remove that threat, should peace talks fail. ... It is also important that the ICC indictments against LRA be acted on
records.political_signal: A dual-track approach is endorsed: political engagement backed by a credible military threat and an unwavering commitment to ICC justice.

records.record_text: The Security Council intends to review the issue of the international protection of the refugee and IDP camps and requests the Secretary-General to provide to it recommendations in this regard
records.political_signal: The Council is formally taking up President Déby's request and initiating a process to assess options for a security presence in Chad.

records.record_text: It is important that the Governments of the Sudan and Chad begin dialogue and implement the measures in the Tripoli Agreement.
records.actor_target: Government of Sudan; Government of Chad

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission on the electoral process in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political Engagement, Situation Assessment, Peace Process Support, UN Mission Oversight
main_risks: Deterioration of the political climate, including hate speech, political intimidation, and limitations on freedoms.
Lack of a level playing field for elections, particularly regarding media access.
Potential for violence and disputes over electoral results.
Fragile security situation, especially in the east, and delays in creating a professional, disciplined national army.
Severe economic mismanagement and corruption, threatening donor confidence and post-electoral stability.
Impunity for human rights violations, including sexual violence, committed by security forces.
main_commitments: Congolese transitional authorities reaffirmed their commitment to holding elections on 30 July 2006.
President Kabila committed to convene a meeting of transitional institutions to build consensus and address political tensions.
The Security Council mission reiterated the international community's commitment to sustained assistance for the electoral and peace processes.
main_policy_signals: Elections must be held on time in a peaceful, fair, and transparent manner.
All parties and candidates must accept the results of the polls and use legal channels for disputes.
Hate speech, ethnic incitement, and intimidation are unacceptable and must be condemned.
Transparent economic management is vital for restoring donor confidence and ensuring post-electoral stability.
Security sector reform, including ending impunity and creating a professional army, is critical for the long-term stability of the country.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission visited Kinshasa from 10-12 June 2006, just weeks before the country's first democratic elections in over four decades. The mission's purpose was to assess the final phase of the transition, convey strong political messages about the conduct of the elections, and evaluate post-electoral challenges. The mission found a highly tense political environment characterized by intimidation, hate speech, and concerns about the fairness of the process. It engaged a wide range of actors, pressing all to ensure a peaceful campaign and respect for the results. The report underscores critical risks related to the political climate, security sector dysfunction, and severe economic mismanagement, while outlining recommendations for Congolese authorities and the international community to mitigate these threats to a successful transition and post-electoral stability.

activities.activity_description: Met with the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the four Vice-Presidents, separately
Met with the bureau of the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC)
Met with a forum grouping members of some of the 273 political parties participating in the electoral process
Met with the bureau of the High Media Authority
Met with the International Committee in Support of the Transition (CIAT)
Met with an ecumenical group of religious leaders
Met with a group of women’s non-governmental organizations focusing on the issue of sexual violence
Met with the representatives of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Met with the local business community represented by members of the Fédération des entreprises du congo (FEC)

Met with Christophe Lutundula, Member of the Parliament of Transition and chairman of the Special Parliamentary Commission in charge of evaluating the legitimacy of the contracts concluded during the 1996-1997 and 1998 conflicts
Met with the Joint Commission on Security Sector Reform

Met separately with the members of the European Union mission of assistance for security sector reform (EUSEC), with the European Union police mission in Kinshasa (EUPOL), as well as with the deputy commander of the European Union standby force
Briefed by the senior leadership of the United Nations Organization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUC)
Received a briefing from the Chairman of the Group of Experts on the arms embargo in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, established pursuant to resolution 1533 (2004), Ibra Déguène Ka
Met, informally, with the staff of MONUC and of the United Nations agencies, funds and programmes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

actors_met.actor_name: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Joseph Kabila)
Four Vice-Presidents of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Bureau of the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC)
Bureau of the High Media Authority
International Committee in Support of the Transition (CIAT)
Christophe Lutundula, Member of the Parliament of Transition
Joint Commission on Security Sector Reform
European Union mission of assistance for security sector reform (EUSEC)
European Union police mission in Kinshasa (EUPOL)
Deputy commander of the European Union standby force
Senior leadership of the United Nations Organization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUC)
Chairman of the Group of Experts on the arms embargo in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Staff of MONUC and of the United Nations agencies, funds and programmes

records.record_text: The Security Council mission stressed the need for the elections to be held in accordance with the calendar announced by IEC, in a peaceful climate free of intimidation, fear and the use of derogatory language.
records.political_signal: The Security Council has a clear expectation for timely and peaceful elections.

records.record_text: While highlighting the strict impartiality and neutrality of the international community in the electoral process, the mission urged the transitional authorities to ensure a level playing field for the elections, including equitable access to the public media for all the parties and candidates.
records.political_signal: The international community's neutrality is conditional on a fair process for all.

records.record_text: The mission also called for the publication of the full electoral timetable, including the dates of the possible second round of the presidential elections and provincial and local elections.
records.policy_implication: Increased transparency and predictability in the electoral process is required.

records.record_text: President Kabila shared the concerns of the members of the Security Council delegation regarding the deterioration of the political climate in the run-up to the elections, including acts of political intimidation and limitations on the freedom of access of some of the smaller political parties to the media.
records.political_signal: The President acknowledges the validity of the mission's key concerns.

records.record_text: President Kabila acknowledged the recent deterioration in the political environment... Some political actors had been encouraging the dissemination of hate messages and the exclusion of some sections of the population from the electoral process. Some media sources were also promoting the potentially dangerous national identity concept termed congolité. He emphasized the commitment of the Government to decisively address these matters.

The electoral process had benefited from substantial international technical, logistical and financial assistance, while insufficient international assistance had been provided for security sector reform.
records.political_signal: Signals a request for rebalancing international support towards SSR.
records.policy_implication: Future international aid packages may need to prioritize SSR.

records.record_text: The Vice-Presidents expressed serious concern at the prevailing climate of intolerance, caused by acts of political intimidation, and the public incitement by some parties along ethnic and nationalist lines, including speculation about the nationalities of some presidential candidates.
Vice-Presidents Bemba, Ruberwa and Z’Ahidi Ngoma called for the convening of a political dialogue among the main institutions of the transition.
records.policy_implication: A formal dialogue could either ease tensions or create delays, a risk noted by the mission in para 50.

records.record_text: Vice-Presidents, in particular Bemba and Ruberwa, emphasized the need to ensure the credibility of the electoral process, including through the impartiality of the Supreme Court and the other Courts, which are to resolve electoral disputes, and the security services.

Vice-President Ruberwa also called for additional efforts, including from MONUC, to address the continued presence of foreign armed groups, in particular the former Forces armées rwandaises (FAR)/Interahamwe in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces the need for continued MONUC FARDC joint operations against foreign armed groups.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission urged IEC to make all possible efforts to minimize the time period between the first and second rounds of the presidential elections, if a second is necessary.
records.political_signal: A prolonged interim period is seen as a source of instability.

records.record_text: The political environment has significantly deteriorated in recent months. Steps needed to be taken urgently to ensure respect for civil liberties, free and equitable access to the media for all of the political parties and candidates, the security of the electorate and candidates, and the integrity of electoral procedures, in particular the counting of votes and announcement of the results;
There is a shortfall of some $46 million in the electoral budget.
records.policy_implication: The electoral process may face operational constraints without additional funding.

records.record_text: The Chairman of the High Media Authority indicated that inadequate support had been received for its operations from the international community and the Transitional Government, which had negatively affected its ability to implement its mandate.
records.policy_implication: The media regulator's effectiveness is compromised, undermining efforts to ensure a level playing field.

records.record_text: The mission also insisted on strict respect for the results of the polls.
records.political_signal: The international community will not tolerate attempts to overturn the democratic will of the people.

records.record_text: Members of CIAT shared the concern of the mission regarding the need for the transitional authorities to ensure continuity in the management of the State in the period following the first round of the presidential elections, should a second round be required.
records.actor_source: International Committee in Support of the Transition (CIAT)
records.policy_implication: A potential power vacuum between election rounds is a major point of concern for key international partners.

records.record_text: The mission expressed deep concern at the reported mismanagement of the economy, including the considerable increase in extrabudgetary expenditures since late in 2005.
records.political_signal: Economic transparency is a core expectation of the Security Council.
records.policy_implication: Continued economic mismanagement could lead to instability and jeopardize international financial support.

records.record_text: The mission noted the suspension by IMF and the World Bank of their respective economic and budgetary assistance programmes owing to concerns regarding the financial mismanagement of the State.
records.policy_implication: The DRC is already facing concrete negative consequences for its lack of fiscal discipline, jeopardizing post-election recovery.

records.record_text: The mission expressed concern at the continued prevalence of incidents of sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, most of which are committed by members of FARDC and the armed groups.

The Congolese authorities and stakeholders of the Democratic Republic of the Congo are encouraged to ensure that the announced date of 30 July, for the holding of the first round of the presidential elections and the national legislative elections, is respected.
records.political_signal: The 30 July election date is non-negotiable from the perspective of the Security Council.

records.record_text: It is critical that the political parties carry out the electoral campaign in accordance with the code of conduct for political parties, as prepared by the Independent Electoral Commission, and that the electoral campaign be conducted in an atmosphere of calm and tolerance. Debates should be focused on the future of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including programmes prepared in the interest of the population. Hate language, incitements to ethnic hatred and exclusion should not be tolerated.
records.political_signal: The Security Council is setting clear red lines on campaign conduct.

records.record_text: Efforts aimed at reforming and restructuring the army, including the integration of coherent units and the administrative reform of the military command structure, need to be urgently pursued.
records.policy_implication: Post-election stability depends on accelerating SSR.

records.record_text: A more systematic effort is required to put an end to impunity within the ranks of the security services by bringing to justice the alleged perpetrators of human rights violations among military and police personnel and relieving higher-ranking officers who show serious leadership deficiencies.
records.policy_implication: Ending impunity is a prerequisite for a professional and accountable security sector.

records.record_text: The international community should be encouraged to increase its support for security sector reform in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The Congolese authorities are encouraged to make efforts to meet the expectations of the international financial institutions with regard to the requirements for the resumption of assistance from IMF and the World Bank.
records.political_signal: The path to resuming crucial IFI assistance is through concrete governance reforms.

records.record_text: The continuation of the functioning of the State and its institutions, including transparent and responsible economic management, in the period between the holding of the first polls and the establishment of the elected Government, is critical to ensuring the stability of the country.

The Government should take steps to address the continued prevalence of sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including taking urgent action to end impunity within the armed forces.

The Mission is encouraged to work with the Department of Peacekeeping Operations as well as the authorities of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to develop specific options for the consideration of the Security Council in its deliberations on its future mandate.
records.political_signal: The Security Council is beginning the process of planning for the post-transition phase of the UN's presence.

mission_title: Report on the visit to Ethiopia and Eritrea by Ambassador Kenzo Oshima

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Fact-finding and Political Engagement
main_risks: Resumption of armed conflict due to military build-up and miscalculation.
Operational paralysis and safety risks for UNMEE personnel due to Eritrean restrictions, particularly the helicopter ban.
Potential for devastating consequences if UNMEE withdraws.
Entrenchment of the political and diplomatic stalemate.
main_commitments: The mission head committed to recommend that the Security Council hasten consideration of a new resolution urging Eritrea to lift restrictions and Ethiopia to accept the Boundary Commission decision.
The mission head committed to recommend that the Council ask the Secretary-General and influential countries to launch new diplomatic initiatives.
main_policy_signals: The Security Council, through the mission, signalled deep concern over the deteriorating situation and its appreciation for UNMEE and TCCs.
Ethiopia signalled its commitment to 'maximum restraint' but also its readiness to act defensively, while seeking a 'practical' implementation of the border decision through dialogue.
Eritrea signalled that 'unintended consequences' could result if the 'main problem'—Ethiopia's non-compliance with the Boundary Commission decision—is not addressed urgently by the Security Council.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Chairman of the Security Council Working Group on Peacekeeping Operations conducted a high-level, short-duration fact-finding mission to Ethiopia and Eritrea to assess a rapidly deteriorating situation. The mission confirmed the tense and volatile environment, with military build-ups on both sides, and the severe operational constraints imposed on UNMEE by Eritrea, which created high risks for peacekeepers and the ceasefire. The mission found the parties' positions to be entrenched and mutually exclusive: Ethiopia calling for dialogue on 'practical' implementation of the border decision, and Eritrea demanding unconditional implementation. The report concludes with urgent recommendations for the Security Council to pass a new resolution demanding compliance from both parties and to support renewed, high-level diplomatic efforts to break the stalemate and avert a return to war.

activities.activity_description: Held extensive discussions with Special Representative Legwaila and his staff.
Received operational briefings on the situation from Major General Rajender Singh and his staff.
Meetings with representatives of countries contributing troops and other military personnel to UNMEE and other members of the diplomatic community in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Met with Seyoum Mesfin, Foreign Minister of Ethiopia, on 7 November.
Paid a visit to Sector East headquarters at Assab, Eritrea, on 8 November.
Met with Colonel Zecarias Ogbagaber, Acting Commissioner, Commission for Coordination with UNMEE in Asmara on 8 November.
Met with Yemane Gebremeskel, Director of the Office of the President of Eritrea in Asmara on 8 November.

actors_met.actor_name: Representatives of countries contributing troops and other military personnel to UNMEE

records.record_text: According to UNMEE, the current situation is tense and potentially volatile and could deteriorate further.

Both Ethiopia and Eritrea have been moving their military forces. Ethiopia has been reinforcing its military in areas adjacent to the Temporary Security Zone, while Eritrea may be doing the same outside the Zone, although UNMEE does not have full capability to verify such movement owing to the restrictions imposed by Eritrea.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates the escalating military tensions and the direct impact of restrictions on mandate implementation.

records.record_text: The restrictions have caused serious problems in terms of both operation and administration, the most serious one being the ban on helicopter flights, which has reduced UNMEE monitoring capabilities by 60 per cent and seriously affected medical evacuations.
records.policy_implication: The restrictions render the mission significantly less effective and endanger its personnel.

records.record_text: I noted the concern of UNMEE that, if the two sides continue to strengthen their military postures, the possibility of the resumption of armed conflict through miscalculation cannot be excluded, given the atmosphere of mutual mistrust.
records.policy_implication: Heightens the urgency for Security Council intervention to de-escalate the situation.

records.record_text: At the meetings held in each capital, the same difficult dilemma was expressed by the contributing countries: while they wish to maintain the presence of their troops and other personnel, who carry out important tasks for UNMEE, the restrictions are impeding the Mission’s operation and putting their personnel at unreasonable risk.
records.policy_implication: Indicates potential for TCC withdrawal if conditions do not improve, which could lead to the collapse of the mission.

records.record_text: There was a unified appeal from the contributing countries for the urgent removal of the restrictions imposed on UNMEE.

At the same time, it was acknowledged that behind the action taken by Eritrea were its frustrations over the refusal of Ethiopia to accept the Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission’s decision unequivocally and to proceed with demarcation of the border without preconditions.
records.policy_implication: Provides context for Eritrea's actions and highlights the root cause of the stalemate according to some observers.

records.record_text: Despite the difficulties faced by UNMEE, many believed that its withdrawal would have devastating consequences.
records.policy_implication: Strengthens the argument for maintaining the mission despite the challenges.

records.record_text: Foreign Minister Seyoum generally reiterated the position...that Ethiopia “accepts in principle” the Boundary Commission’s decision as final and binding.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia maintains its official stance of acceptance, but the qualification 'in principle' is the core of the dispute.

records.record_text: In response to my request for clarification, the Minister emphasized that Ethiopia was not asking for partial or total renegotiation of the decision, but rather believed that the decision should be implemented in a practical rather than a mechanical manner, pointing to locations to be reviewed since both Ethiopian as well as Eritrean communities and villages would be affected.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia is seeking dialogue and adjustments to the demarcation process, which Eritrea rejects as a precondition.
records.policy_implication: This position is the central point of the stalemate, as it contradicts Eritrea's demand for unconditional implementation.

records.record_text: When I conveyed the Security Council’s concern over the situation, he stated that Ethiopia would exercise maximum restraint, neither being the first party to open fire nor allowing itself to be provoked.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia seeks to reassure the Security Council of its defensive posture and lack of intent to initiate hostilities.

records.record_text: The Minister, criticizing Eritrea for blackmailing the Council through the imposition of restrictions on the Mission’s freedom of movement, emphasized that the Council must not act in ways that would have the effect of rewarding Eritrea’s actions.
records.political_signal: Ethiopia is attempting to frame Council action, warning against any perceived concessions to Eritrea.

records.record_text: Yemane Gebremeskel stated that the current difficulties were a direct result of the violation by Ethiopia, namely, its refusal to accept the Boundary Commission’s decision as final and binding and to fully comply with it.
records.political_signal: Eritrea places the full blame for the crisis on Ethiopia's non-compliance.

records.record_text: He criticized the Security Council for ignoring for too long the main reason for the stalemate and for failing to compel Ethiopia to accept the border ruling as provided in the Algiers Agreements and to proceed with demarcation without preconditions.
records.political_signal: Eritrea is expressing deep frustration with the Council's perceived inaction and partiality.
records.policy_implication: This explains Eritrea's rationale for taking unilateral action (restricting UNMEE) to force the issue onto the Council's agenda.

records.record_text: He rejected the idea of a special envoy of the Secretary-General, saying that it would violate the Algiers Agreements. He also rejected the expansion of the mandate of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General to include political matters.
records.political_signal: Eritrea closes off potential avenues for dialogue or mediation that it views as outside the strict framework of the Algiers Agreements.

records.record_text: He said that Eritrea wanted a peaceful solution but warned that unintended consequences could result unless the main problem was addressed promptly.
records.political_signal: This is a veiled threat that the situation could escalate to conflict if Eritrea's core demands are not met.

records.record_text: The current stalemate is filled with risk, and any incidents resulting therefrom may cause further deterioration in the situation.
To avoid the resumption of hostilities between Ethiopia and Eritrea, the Security Council needs to give serious attention to the question of how to help break the stalemate;

The restrictions on UNMEE and, in particular, the ban on helicopter flights, which are a clear violation of the Algiers Agreements and seriously impede the Mission’s operational capabilities and put its personnel at risk, should be removed as quickly as possible.
records.policy_implication: The mission validates UNMEE's and TCCs' concerns, branding the restrictions a treaty violation.

records.record_text: In view of the difficulties and risks faced by UNMEE and the contributing countries, the Security Council must hasten consideration of a new resolution urging in the strongest terms that Eritrea lift the restrictions;
Full acceptance of and compliance with the Boundary Commission’s decision by Ethiopia must be achieved urgently. Failure to do so would be a violation of the Algiers Agreements.
records.policy_implication: The mission report formally identifies Ethiopia's failure to comply as a violation, balancing the criticism of Eritrea.

records.record_text: In this regard, the new resolution should urge Ethiopia, for its part, to fully accept and implement the decision;
records.political_signal: Recommends a balanced approach for the Security Council, with specific demands placed on both parties.

records.record_text: At the same time, the Council should ask the Secretary-General and the countries that have influence on the two parties to launch a new series of vigorous diplomatic initiatives to break the stalemate.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Central Africa, 4 to 11 November 2005
mission_country_or_region: Central Africa (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Uganda, Rwanda, United Republic of Tanzania)

main_risks: Failure to meet the 30 June 2006 electoral deadline in the DRC.
Continued destabilization of eastern DRC and the region by foreign armed groups (FDLR, LRA, FNL).
Lack of capacity and logistical failures within the newly integrated Congolese army (FARDC), particularly regarding salary payments.
Potential for political instability in post-transition Burundi and risk of premature withdrawal of UN peacekeepers.
Ongoing violations of the arms embargo on DRC and insufficient regional cooperation to stop it.
main_commitments: The DRC transitional authorities reaffirmed their commitment to the electoral timeline.
The Government of Burundi agreed to a gradual, negotiated disengagement of the ONUB peacekeeping mission.
Regional presidents (Uganda, Rwanda) expressed support for the DRC elections but insisted on the need to resolve the issue of armed groups.
The Governments of Uganda and Rwanda made commitments to improve cooperation with the UN Group of Experts and strengthen border controls.
main_policy_signals: The Security Council's insistence on holding DRC elections before the 30 June 2006 deadline is non-negotiable.
An inclusive political process in the DRC is highly encouraged, but not at the expense of the electoral timeline.
The international community's continued support for Burundi is assured, but a premature withdrawal of UN peacekeepers would be a mistake.
Cross-border military incursions without the host state's consent are a violation of the UN Charter (a direct message to Uganda).
The Council is focused on the link between armed groups, the arms embargo, and illegal exploitation of natural resources, and expects full regional cooperation.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission conducted a high-level, multi-country engagement at a critical juncture for the Great Lakes region. The primary focus was to apply political pressure on the Democratic Republic of the Congo to adhere to the electoral timeline, while also assessing security challenges posed by foreign armed groups. The mission engaged a wide array of actors, from heads of state to civil society, and undertook field visits beyond capital cities. It effectively delivered strong political messages regarding electoral deadlines, regional security responsibilities, and respect for sovereignty. The mission also evaluated the transition in Burundi from peacekeeping to peacebuilding, cautioning against a premature withdrawal of ONUB. Overall, it was a comprehensive review and political signalling exercise, highlighting the interconnectedness of political and security issues across the region and aiming to shape the future actions of both regional states and the Security Council itself.

activities.activity_description: Visit to Kinshasa, Mbuji-Mayi and Kamina in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Bujumbura, Kigali, Entebbe (Uganda) and Dar es Salaam from 4 to 11 November 2005.
Met with the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Joseph Kabila.
Met with the President of Burundi, Pierre Nkurunziza.
Met with the President of Uganda, Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
Met with the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame.
Met with the President of the United Republic of Tanzania, Benjamin Mkapa.
Met separately with the four Vice-Presidents of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Kinshasa.
Met with the Presidents of the National Assembly and the Senate in Kinshasa.
Met with the Chairman and members of the standing committee of the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) and the Chairman of the Media High Authority in Kinshasa.
Met with the Joint Commission on Security Sector Reform in Kinshasa.
Met with representatives of civil society and religious organizations in Kinshasa.
Met with a group of women ministers and parliamentarians in Kinshasa.
Met with the International Committee in Support of the Transition (CIAT).
Held informal discussions with the leadership of the opposition political party, the Union pour la démocratie et le progrès social (UDPS).
Met in Mbuji-Mayi with the Governor of Kasai Oriental Province, the local representative of IEC and members of the Provincial Security Committee.
Visited the military base of Kamina (Katanga Province), where it received a comprehensive briefing on the military integration process.
Held consultations with a Government delegation led by the Minister of External Relations and Cooperation in Bujumbura.
Met with the leadership of the main political parties represented in Parliament in Burundi: FRODEBU, UPRONA, and CNDD-FDD.
Head of the mission met informally with the former Head of State, Domitien Ndayizeye.
Met with civil society organizations working on transitional justice and judicial reform in Burundi.
Received briefings from the United Nations Organization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUC) in Kinshasa, Mbuji-Mayi and Kamina.
Received briefing from the United Nations Operation in Burundi (ONUB) in Bujumbura.
Met with the Minister for Foreign Affairs in Dar es Salaam.
Received briefings from the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for the Great Lakes Region, Ibrahima Fall.
Received briefing from the Chairman of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ibra Déguène Ka.
Met with United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations based in the United Republic of Tanzania to discuss the issue of refugees.
Met with the academic community of Dar es Salaam.
Was briefed on the actions MONUC and ONUB had taken to address cases and allegations of sexual exploitation and abuse.
Discussed resolution 1325 (2000) on women and peace and security, in Kinshasa with non-governmental organizations and women members of Parliament, and in Bujumbura with the ONUB gender adviser.
Was briefed on the efforts undertaken by MONUC and ONUB regarding child protection.
