records.record_text: One of the primary objectives of this, the fourth mission of the Security Council to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries, was to encourage the Congolese parties to put into practice, with the least possible further delay, the global and all inclusive accord on the establishment of a transitional government for the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: The mission's primary goal was to accelerate the implementation of the peace accord.

records.record_text: While the Security Council mission noted the progress made so far, members also manifested their disappointment at the slow pace of implementation.
records.political_signal: The Council is dissatisfied with the lack of progress.
records.policy_implication: Increased pressure on the parties may be forthcoming.

records.record_text: In the view of the Security Council mission, the time for war had passed and the time had come to carry out the political agreements the parties had already signed.
records.political_signal: There is no military solution; parties must adhere to their political commitments.

records.record_text: The international community, which looked forward to contributing to the reconstruction of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, would be better able to increase its support when a transitional Government was in place.
records.political_signal: International reconstruction assistance is conditioned on the formation of the transitional government.
records.policy_implication: Financial and technical support will be withheld or delayed until political progress is made.

records.record_text: Accordingly, the mission registered its expectation with all the parties concerned that a functioning transitional Congolese Government would be set up by 30 June, with a unified national army capable of the defence of its national borders and population, and a developing economy in control of the country’s natural resources.
records.political_signal: The mission set a clear and public deadline for the formation of the transitional government.
records.policy_implication: Failure to meet the deadline could trigger further Council action.

records.record_text: However, the remaining steps to be taken may well prove among the most difficult.
records.policy_implication: The final stages of forming the government are anticipated to be highly contentious.

records.record_text: The mission expects the Congolese parties to establish a functioning transitional Government by 30 June 2003, in accordance with undertakings provided to the mission during its visit to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: This is a direct demand for action, not just an expectation.

records.record_text: The mission also made clear its deep concern at the persistent fighting that continued to afflict Bunia and North and South Kivu, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
This fighting was not only inconsistent with the quest for a political solution, it also posed the risk that political agreements might be undermined and their credibility called into question.
records.political_signal: Continued fighting threatens to derail the entire peace process.

records.record_text: All parties should therefore cease all hostile military activity.
The mission, in its meetings and contacts, called for all parties in North Kivu to withdraw their forces to the positions previously agreed.

Furthermore, the gross and widespread violations of human rights that have accompanied the fighting in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo... were cause for extreme dismay and should be stopped forthwith.
records.political_signal: The Council is appalled by the human rights situation and demands it stop immediately.
records.policy_implication: This signals a focus on accountability for these violations.

records.record_text: It was also noted that these problems were exacerbated by influence from neighbouring countries.
records.policy_implication: The Council sees regional dynamics as a key driver of the conflict.

records.record_text: The mission felt that, if properly conceived, the international conference could help to address and resolve the long-term peace and security issues, following the necessary progress of the peace process in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi.
records.policy_implication: Support for the conference is conditioned on progress in national peace processes.

records.record_text: The mission was struck by the depopulation of some parts of the city, as well as the highly visible presence of child soldiers it observed in the streets as it passed.
The mission is aware that it is the Union des patriotes congolais (UPC) that holds and surrounds the town of Bunia and currently controls the access routes.
records.policy_implication: Identifies UPC as the primary military actor in Bunia, implying their responsibility for the situation.

records.record_text: All the mission’s various interlocutors throughout the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the region as a whole expressed support for IEMF.
records.policy_implication: There is broad political backing for the IEMF intervention.

records.record_text: The mission was impressed by the dignity and sense of commitment conveyed by these two representatives of the interim administration, which currently represents the sole source of legitimate authority in the Ituri region.
records.political_signal: The mission endorses the Ituri interim administration as a legitimate partner.

records.record_text: The mission, noting the actions already taken that had culminated in the deployment of MONUC and of IEMF, expressed the view that the problems of Ituri could best be resolved in the context of the broader political agreement to be reached in Kinshasa among the Congolese parties, so that Iturian issues, institutions and actors could be integrated into the national transitional political process.
records.political_signal: The mission rejects a separate or isolated solution for Ituri, insisting on its integration into the national framework.

records.record_text: Some of the mission’s interlocutors pointed out that if MONUC was to take over from IEMF as from 2 September, it should be given, at least for a limited period of time, the same mandate and means as IEMF. Otherwise, MONUC would not enjoy the necessary credibility in the eyes of the local militias.
records.policy_implication: There is a strong push from actors on the ground for a 'Chapter VII' mandate for MONUC in Ituri to ensure a seamless and credible transition from IEMF.

records.record_text: Furthermore, the mission’s interlocutors pointed out that while IEMF would, during the period of its deployment, provide Bunia with stability, the rest of Ituri would remain vulnerable to the activities of the various militias.
records.policy_implication: The security 'bubble' created by IEMF in Bunia does not address the wider insecurity in the Ituri region.

records.record_text: The mission therefore called on those of its interlocutors in the region with influence on the armed groups and militias to exert pressure in favour of a cessation of hostilities and the restoration of calm.
records.political_signal: The mission is holding regional states responsible for controlling the militias they influence.

records.record_text: The mission noted further that the return of stability in Bunia could not depend purely on a military approach. ... A political settlement was urgently required.
records.policy_implication: Military force is a temporary fix; a long-term solution requires political action.

records.record_text: The States of the region should take all necessary measures to end the supply of arms to militias and armed groups, and countries should use their positive influence to prevail upon the militias and armed groups to abandon the military option and participate in the political process.
records.political_signal: This is a direct call on regional states to stop fueling the conflict.
records.policy_implication: The Council is considering measures against states that continue to arm militias, such as an arms embargo.

records.record_text: Some members mentioned the possibility that the Security Council might have to consider whether MONUC should have two separate mandates — on the one hand a variable mandate for Ituri and Bunia, and on the other a mandate for the rest of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.policy_implication: The Council is internally debating a differentiated approach to MONUC's mandate, potentially giving it more robust capabilities in Ituri than elsewhere.

records.record_text: The mission found Bunia, for the moment, calm but tense.
records.political_signal: The stability brought by IEMF is fragile and potentially temporary.

records.record_text: For its part, the mission sees a clear need for the demilitarization of Bunia; for the securing of the city by an IEMF/MONUC capable of maintaining order...; for control of the access roads...; for the provision of support and protection to the interim institutions...; and for the expansion, albeit gradual, into Ituri as a whole of the authority of the interim administration in secure conditions.
records.policy_implication: This outlines a multi-pronged strategy for stabilizing Ituri that the Council is likely to adopt, influencing the future MONUC mandate.

records.record_text: Many of the mission’s interlocutors expressed support for this approach [imposing an arms embargo on Ituri], and some stressed that in order to be effective an embargo should be enforced and monitored.
records.policy_implication: There is support on the ground for an arms embargo, with an emphasis on the need for an enforcement mechanism.

records.record_text: The offensive launched by RCD (Goma) in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo thus represents not only a violation of the agreements but also a threat to the pursuit of the political process, and the mission vigorously condemns it.
records.political_signal: The Council strongly denounces RCD-Goma's military actions as unacceptable spoilers to the peace process.
records.policy_implication: RCD-Goma may face targeted measures from the Council.

records.record_text: Members of the mission who met with RCD (Goma) representatives in Kinshasa demanded that it cease hostilities forthwith and withdraw its forces to the positions earlier agreed.

The military offensives conducted by RCD (Goma) in North and South Kivu are particularly damaging to MONUC’s voluntary disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and resettlement or repatriation operations, many of which have been disrupted by military activity.

Members of the mission drew the particular attention of RCD (Goma) representatives, and subsequently of the Rwandan Government, to their views on these disruptions, which seemed to go far beyond coincidence.
records.political_signal: The mission implies that RCD-Goma, with potential Rwandan backing, is deliberately sabotaging DDRRR efforts.
records.policy_implication: The Council is linking RCD-Goma's actions to its patron, Rwanda, and holding both accountable.

records.record_text: It is they [the de facto local authorities] who will be held accountable for any failure to proceed rapidly with disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and resettlement or repatriation.
records.political_signal: Responsibility for DDRRR success is placed squarely on local armed group leaders, with a clear threat of consequences for failure.

records.record_text: The mission stressed to all its interlocutors that impunity would no longer be tolerated, and that those responsible for crimes should expect to be held accountable for them.
records.political_signal: The era of impunity is over; accountability for international crimes is now a core priority for the Council.
records.policy_implication: This signals Council support for judicial mechanisms, potentially including international tribunals or sanctions against perpetrators.

records.record_text: The mission considers leaders responsible for the acts of their followers, particularly when the parties concerned are the de facto local authorities and where the mission is aware of no evidence of any action taken by those authorities to prevent or punish the crimes in question.
records.political_signal: The principle of command responsibility will be applied to leaders of armed groups in the DRC.
records.policy_implication: Leaders of factions like UPC and RCD-Goma are being put on notice that they can be held personally liable for atrocities committed by their troops.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council be prepared to pledge its full support to the transitional Government to be established in the Democratic Republic of the Congo by 30 June 2003.

The mission recommends that the Council be prepared to call on bilateral and multilateral donors to render all possible assistance in the reconstruction of the country, including in the development of a capable unified armed forces and police service, and to promote its further development by all possible means and on an urgent basis.
records.policy_implication: The mission advocates for international assistance in security sector reform (SSR) as a key component of reconstruction.

records.record_text: The mission is deeply concerned, not only by the present situation in Bunia but also by the possibility of further fighting, humanitarian catastrophe and human rights violations after the current emergency measures expire on 1 September.
records.political_signal: The mission is flagging the post-IEMF security gap as a top-priority risk that requires an urgent Council decision.

records.record_text: The mission recommends to the Security Council that it increase pressure on the parties, both in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and throughout the region, to ensure that the necessary guarantees are provided to MONUC to permit its verification activities.
records.policy_implication: MONUC's verification mandate is being obstructed, and the mission wants the Council to use its political weight to ensure compliance.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that consideration be given to what practical steps can be taken to end impunity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi.
records.policy_implication: The mission is asking the Council to move from political statements on impunity to designing concrete accountability mechanisms.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council be prepared to consider carefully and act on the recommendations to be made by the Expert Panel in its forthcoming report.
records.policy_implication: The Council is being primed to take action, possibly including sanctions, based on the findings of the expert panel on illegal exploitation of resources.

records.record_text: The mission will continue to reflect on the impressions it formed during its visit to Bunia, in the light of the success of IEMF and of subsequent developments, in order to define what could be the most effective role for MONUC in the Democratic Republic of the Congo peace process, including the possibility of a more robust mandate, taking into account the departure of IEMF.
records.policy_implication: A decision on strengthening MONUC's mandate is pending further deliberation by the Council.

records.record_text: The Security Council will continue to follow closely the roles and activities of the States of the region in the light of the responsibilities borne by those States to assist the Congolese parties and the international community by using their positive influence to find peaceful solutions to the conflict both in Ituri and in the wider Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: Regional states are under continued Security Council scrutiny regarding their role in the DRC conflict.

records.record_text: The objective of the mission was to demonstrate the support of the Council for the second phase of the political transition, at a time when the peace process was facing particular challenges.
records.political_signal: The Council's visit was intended to bolster a fragile transitional period in Burundi.

records.record_text: The mission stressed that the transitional institutions should continue to undertake the reforms as provided for in the Arusha Agreement, particularly in the security sector, the judiciary and the organization of the elections.
All the interlocutors of the mission, both national and international, stressed that the continuation of fighting was the most serious obstacle to the full implementation of the Arusha peace process.
records.policy_implication: There is a universal view on the ground that ending the fighting is the number one priority.

records.record_text: The mission expressed concern at the very slow pace of ceasefire negotiations between the Government and FDD and FNL.
The mission called on the rebel groups to cease hostilities immediately and join the Arusha process.
records.actor_target: Front pour la défense de la démocratie (FDD) (Pierre Nkurunziza)

records.record_text: The mission emphasized that the solution of the conflict was to be found in the political process provided by the Arusha Agreement. The mission reminded the rebel groups that there were no alternative processes and that joining the Arusha process was in their own interest.
records.actor_target: Front pour la défense de la démocratie (FDD) (Pierre Nkurunziza)
records.political_signal: The Arusha Agreement is the only game in town; rebel groups will not be offered a separate or parallel peace process.

records.record_text: The mission encouraged the transitional Government to put in place measures to enable some FDD combatants in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to be repatriated voluntarily to Burundi.
records.policy_implication: The mission is proposing a specific confidence-building measure to advance the peace process.

records.record_text: They [AMIB] indicated that the preparation of the cantonment sites was seriously hampered by the failure of the parties to provide the location and troop strength to the Joint Ceasefire Commission (JCC).
records.policy_implication: Lack of cooperation from the conflict parties is preventing the implementation of key ceasefire provisions.

records.record_text: The mission reiterated the Council’s continued support for AMIB on three levels: political support from the Council, financial support from the donor community and technical support from the United Nations Secretariat.
records.political_signal: The Security Council is fully behind the African Union's peacekeeping effort in Burundi.

records.record_text: The transitional Government asked the mission to respond positively to the request of the transitional Government for the establishment of an international judiciary commission of inquiry, as provided for in the Arusha Agreement, to help Burundi put an end to impunity.
records.policy_implication: The Burundian government is formally requesting UN assistance in establishing a truth and/or justice mechanism.

records.record_text: The humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate alarmingly.

The mission acknowledges that there should be some dividends to peace and indicates that it will follow closely the results of the donor conference to be organized in September by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) aimed at clearing Burundi’s arrears.
records.policy_implication: The mission recognizes the link between economic support and the sustainability of the peace process.

records.record_text: The Burundi peace process is at a critical juncture. Every effort should be made to ensure its success.
records.policy_implication: The mission is highlighting the high stakes and fragility of the process.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council call on the international financial community to assist AMIB with adequate financial and logistical assistance and on the Secretary-General to provide appropriate expertise.
records.policy_implication: The Council is being asked to lead resource mobilization efforts for the AU mission.

records.record_text: There is a risk that all the gains achieved so far could collapse if such assistance [budgetary and economic support] is not provided immediately.
records.policy_implication: The mission warns of state collapse and a reversal of the peace process due to economic failure.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Council urge donor countries to fulfil the commitments they made at the Paris and Geneva conferences.
records.policy_implication: The Council is being asked to apply political pressure on donors to disburse pledged funds.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission notes that urgent attention should be paid to putting an end to impunity in Burundi. The mission recommends that the Security Council assist Burundi in this regard and that it consider carefully the Government’s request for the establishment of the international judicial commission of inquiry as provided for in the Arusha Agreement.
records.policy_implication: The mission endorses the Burundian government's request and recommends the Council act on it.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission to Kosovo and Belgrade, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: UN Mission Oversight, Implementation Review, Political Engagement
main_risks: The overall situation remains fragile despite progress.
Lack of local ownership of the 'standards before status' benchmarks by provisional institutions.
Slow pace of sustainable minority returns and lack of security and freedom of movement for minorities.
Aspirations for independence and challenges to UNMIK's authority from Kosovo Albanian leaders.
Pervasive influence of organized crime and institutionalized corruption.
Potential for serious economic decline as international aid and presence decrease.
Deep ethnic divisions and lack of reconciliation, with political discourse often divided along ethnic lines.
main_commitments: The Security Council will ultimately determine Kosovo's final status.
The Mission committed to studying information on missing persons and taking appropriate action.
UNMIK was requested to regularly inform the Council on the issue of missing persons.
The Mission confirmed that continued substantial international engagement in Kosovo will be necessary.
main_policy_signals: Strong and consistent endorsement of the 'standards before status' policy as the only viable way forward.
Rejection of any unilateral steps to determine Kosovo's final status.
Support for a unified, multi-ethnic, and integrated Kosovo, with the majority community bearing responsibility for the minority's well-being.
Insistence on the elimination of parallel structures and the integration of all communities into the provisional institutions.
Support for UNMIK's extension of authority throughout Kosovo, particularly in northern Mitrovica.
Call for the start of direct dialogue between Pristina and Belgrade on practical matters.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission assessed that notable progress had been made since its previous visit, particularly in establishing provisional institutions, improving security, and initiating minority returns. However, it found the situation to be fragile, marked by deep ethnic divisions, a slow pace of returns, and a lack of local ownership over the reform process. The mission's primary objective was to reinforce the 'standards before status' policy, which it consistently conveyed to all parties as the only path towards a discussion on final status. It strongly supported UNMIK's work, including its efforts to assert authority in northern Mitrovica, and called for greater responsibility from Kosovo's leaders in building a multi-ethnic society. The mission also urged a direct dialogue between Pristina and Belgrade on practical issues and concluded that a substantial international presence would remain necessary for the foreseeable future.

activities.activity_description: Briefing by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Michael Steiner.

Briefings by the Principal Deputy Special Representative and Deputy Special Representatives of the UNMIK pillars (police and justice, civil administration, institution-building, economic reconstruction).

Meeting with representatives of the provisional institutions of self-government: President Ibrahim Rugova, Prime Minister Bajram Rexhepi, Assembly President Nexhat Daci, and Inter-Ministerial Coordinator for Returns Milorad Todorovic.
Meeting with representatives of the Kosovo Assembly, including members of major Kosovo Albanian political parties, the Kosovo Serb coalition (Povratak), and other ethnic communities.
Meeting with families of missing persons from the Kosovo Albanian community.
Briefing on the security situation by the KFOR Commander, Lieutenant General Fabio Mini, at KFOR headquarters.
Visit to Mitrovica.
Briefing on the Kosovo Trust Agency and the process towards privatization by the Deputy Special Representative for Economic Reconstruction.
Meeting with representatives of Kosovo Serb and Bosniac civil society in Mitrovica.
Briefing from the Special Representative, and the Regional and Municipal Administrators of Mitrovica on the UNMIK presence in northern Mitrovica.
Meeting with the Presidents of the Municipal Assemblies in Mitrovica region (Leposavic, Mitrovica, Srbica, Vucitrn, Zubin Potok, Zvecan).
Visit to the Kosovo Police Service School in Vucitrn.
Briefing by the Director of the KPS School, the Police Commissioner, and a high-ranking KPS officer.
Meeting with a multi-ethnic group of KPS officers.
Meeting with leaders of returnees from Kosovo Albanian and Kosovo Serb communities and the Municipal Assembly President in the Gnjilane municipality.
Meeting with representatives of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and non-governmental organizations.
Visit to the Pristina Municipal Assembly and meeting with deputies from various political parties.
Meeting with a group of Kosovo women representing different ethnic communities, members of the political establishment and civil society.
Joint press conference with the Special Representative at Pristina.
Meeting in Belgrade with the President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Vojislav Kostunica.
Meeting in Belgrade with the Prime Minister of Serbia, Zoran Djindjic.
Meeting in Belgrade with the Deputy Prime Minister of Serbia and President of the Coordination Centre for Kosovo and Metohija, Nebojsa Covic.
Meeting in Belgrade with representatives of the Serbian Association of Families of Missing Persons.
Meeting in Belgrade with the Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs, Goran Svilanovic.
Press conference at Belgrade.

records.record_text: Since the last mission of the Security Council to Kosovo, the Mission finds notable progress in several areas as regards the implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999).
The Mission holds the view that 'standards before status' is the only viable way forward.
records.political_signal: The mission strongly endorsed the existing international policy framework, rejecting calls from some Kosovo Albanian leaders for simultaneous status discussions or early independence.
records.policy_implication: The timeline for addressing Kosovo's final status is conditional on tangible progress in meeting a set of internationally defined benchmarks, particularly regarding rule of law and minority rights.

records.record_text: The Mission has the firm impression that local ownership and commitment to these processes has been less than could have been expected.
records.policy_implication: Progress in Kosovo is overly reliant on the international community, posing a risk to the sustainability of reforms and institutional development.

records.record_text: It is the opinion of the Mission that the time has come for cooperation between Pristina and Belgrade on practical issues.
records.actor_target: Kosovo Provisional Institutions, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Authorities, UNMIK
records.political_signal: The mission is signalling a shift in focus towards normalizing relations through technical cooperation, bypassing the stalemated political dialogue on status.
records.policy_implication: UNMIK is expected to take a more active role in facilitating direct contacts between Pristina and Belgrade.

records.record_text: In the light of the many difficult issues yet to be resolved, the Mission is of the view that continued substantial international engagement in Kosovo will be necessary for the foreseeable future.
records.policy_implication: This serves as a justification for the continued presence and resource allocation for UNMIK and KFOR, countering any suggestions of a premature withdrawal.

records.record_text: ...in spite of these positive developments, the situation remains fragile in Kosovo.
records.policy_implication: The fragility of the situation justifies continued international oversight and presence.

records.record_text: The sustainable return of minorities is a precondition for a multi-ethnic society.
records.political_signal: Sustainable returns are framed as a core benchmark of progress for the entire Kosovo project, not just a humanitarian issue.

records.record_text: The establishment of UNMIK administration in the northern part of Mitrovica has been necessary for the implementation of a uniform standard of administration throughout Kosovo and marks an important move against parallel institutions.
records.political_signal: The mission unequivocally backed UNMIK's assertion of authority against Serb-run parallel structures, reinforcing the policy of a single, unified administrative framework for all of Kosovo.

records.record_text: UNMIK is requested to keep the Council regularly informed.
records.policy_implication: This establishes a formal reporting requirement for UNMIK on the specific issue of missing persons, elevating its prominence on the Council's agenda.

records.record_text: Some believed that placing standards before status was ineffective — rather both should be pursued simultaneously.
records.political_signal: This represents the core disagreement between the Kosovo Albanian leadership and the international community's established policy on the path to final status.

records.record_text: The Kosovo Serb population had little reason to be satisfied with the degree of progress, since two thirds of the Kosovo Serb population remained displaced.
records.actor_source: Milorad Todorovic, Inter-Ministerial Coordinator for Returns
records.political_signal: This position highlights the starkly different perceptions of progress between the majority and minority communities.

records.record_text: The Yugoslav and Serbian authorities... supported the 'standards before status' approach.
records.political_signal: Belgrade's alignment with the international community's policy serves to delay final status talks, which is in its strategic interest.

records.record_text: The Mission appealed to Belgrade to encourage Kosovo Serbs to be constructive partners in these institutions.
records.political_signal: The mission acknowledged Belgrade's influence over the Kosovo Serb community and sought its cooperation in promoting integration over boycott.

records.record_text: One of the main challenges following the establishment of the provisional institutions was managing the aspirations of the Kosovo Albanians for independence and staving off challenges to the authority of UNMIK during the interim period.
records.policy_implication: The fundamental tension between the provisional institutions' desire for sovereignty and UNMIK's mandate under 1244 is a primary source of political friction and a risk to stability.

records.record_text: No unilateral steps will determine Kosovo’s final status. The United Nations Security Council will, in consultation with all concerned, ultimately determine Kosovo’s final status.
records.political_signal: This is a direct assertion of the Security Council's ultimate authority over the final status process, intended to curb any attempts by local actors to pre-empt or dictate the outcome.
records.policy_implication: Any resolution of Kosovo's status must pass through the Security Council, giving its permanent members a de facto veto.

records.record_text: Parallel institutions have no future; integration is the only way forward.
records.actor_target: Kosovo Serb Community, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Authorities
records.political_signal: This message is a clear rejection of any form of partition or separate governance structures for Kosovo Serbs, insisting on their participation within the UNMIK-established framework.

records.record_text: The Mission points to the need for regional cooperation in order to, for example, effectively combat organized crime, including trafficking.
As the majority, Kosovo Albanians must take responsibility for the security of members of minorities and their full access to public services.
records.political_signal: This places the onus for creating a multi-ethnic society directly on the majority population and its leaders, making their actions a key metric for the international community.
records.policy_implication: Failure to ensure minority rights and security could be used as a reason to delay the final status process.

records.record_text: The Mission urges UNMIK, in consultation with local institutions and elected representatives, to further elaborate the proposal for a decentralization of competences to municipalities without delay.
records.policy_implication: Decentralization is identified as a key policy tool to address minority concerns and improve local governance, and the mission wants to see it prioritized.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region, 27 April-7 May 2002

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political Engagement, Peace Process Support, Implementation Review
main_risks: Lack of a fully inclusive political agreement in the DRC post-Sun City.
Partial and unverified withdrawal of foreign forces from the DRC.
Continued fighting in Burundi jeopardizing the Arusha peace process.
Severe economic and humanitarian conditions undermining peace processes in both DRC and Burundi.
Lack of economic 'peace dividends' for the population, risking the credibility of the peace process and the international community.
main_commitments: The mission initiated further discussions among Congolese parties (GoDRC, MLC, RCD-Goma) to achieve a comprehensive agreement.
The mission committed to follow up with international financial institutions regarding donor commitments to Burundi.
The mission committed the Security Council to follow up on the next report of the Panel of Experts on illegal exploitation of natural resources.
main_policy_signals: The dispatch of the mission demonstrated the Security Council's continued commitment to the Great Lakes region.
The mission stressed the need for a fully inclusive power-sharing agreement in the DRC.
The mission clearly signaled that the Security Council would severely condemn any party that violated the ceasefire in the DRC.
The mission demanded the immediate and unconditional demilitarization of Kisangani.
The mission warned armed groups in Burundi to cease hostilities immediately or face potential 'robust measures' from the region.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: This was the third Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region, intended to sustain momentum in the peace processes for the DRC and Burundi. The mission engaged extensively with heads of state, armed groups, UN personnel, and civil society across ten cities. Its primary goals were to support the inter-Congolese dialogue after the Sun City talks, press for the withdrawal of foreign troops from the DRC, advance the disarmament of armed groups (DDRRR), and urge a ceasefire in Burundi. The mission actively brokered discussions, proposed innovative solutions like a 'curtain' of troops for border security, and delivered strong political messages regarding the demilitarization of Kisangani and ceasefire violations. It highlighted the dire humanitarian and economic situation as a major risk to stability and called for urgent international support. The report's recommendations focused on concrete next steps for the Council, including supporting a follow-up mechanism, expanding MONUC's future mandate, and intensifying pressure on belligerents.

activities.activity_description: Visited Johannesburg, Pretoria, Harare, Kinshasa, Kisangani, Luanda, Kampala, Dar es Salaam, Bujumbura and Kigali.
Met with the President of South Africa, Thabo Mbeki.
Met with the President of Zimbabwe, Robert Mugabe.
Met with the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Joseph Kabila.
Met with the President of Angola, José Eduardo dos Santos.
Met with the President of Uganda, Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
Met with the President of the United Republic of Tanzania, Benjamin Mkapa.
Met with the President of Burundi, Pierre Buyoya.
Met with the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame.

Met in Pretoria with the Deputy President of South Africa, Jacob Zuma; the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Gabon, Jean Ping; the President of the Rassemblement congolais pour la démocratie (RCD-Goma), Adolphe Onusumba, and its Secretary-General, Azarias Ruberwa; and, in the presence of the facilitation, with Burundian rebel groups.
In Luanda, the mission met with the Chairman of the Political Committee, the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Angola, Jõao Bernardo de Miranda, and held a joint meeting with the Political Committee.
In Kampala, met with the leader of the Mouvement de libération du Congo (MLC), Jean-Pierre Bemba.

In Pretoria, the mission met with the Chairman and two members of the Panel of Experts on the Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources and Other Forms of Wealth of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
In Bujumbura and Kigali, the mission met with senior ministers of the Governments of Burundi and Rwanda, and with the Implementation Monitoring Committee.
Met with representatives of civil society in Kinshasa and Kisangani, including participants from human rights and religious groups.
Unscheduled informal encounters with local residents that followed [the meeting with civil society in Kisangani].
