records.record_text: The Council had however decided to demonstrate its commitment to the peace processes in the Great Lakes region by dispatching the mission as scheduled.
records.political_signal: The Security Council remains focused on and committed to the Great Lakes peace processes despite other global crises.
records.policy_implication: null

records.record_text: According to this approach, there were three main aspects to the conflict, all mutually interlinked, which had to be taken forward in parallel, namely, the outcome of the inter-Congolese dialogue, the withdrawal of foreign forces from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the disarmament, demobilization and repatriation of the armed groups listed in the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement.
records.political_signal: The mission communicated its analytical framework for resolving the conflict, emphasizing the interconnectedness of political, security, and DDR aspects.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council's approach requires parallel progress on all three tracks; failure in one area will impede progress in others.

records.record_text: Since no comprehensive agreement was reached, however, the Security Council mission also underlined the need for further talks among the Congolese parties in order to develop a fully inclusive agreement on the transition.
records.political_signal: The outcome of the Sun City dialogue is insufficient, and an all-inclusive agreement is a prerequisite for a successful transition.
records.policy_implication: The Council will not accept a partial political settlement and will press for continued negotiations.

records.record_text: The idea was for the creation of a “curtain” of troops along the eastern borders of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, subject to the invitation of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This might involve the parties concerned...to work out mechanisms for military cooperation along their common borders so as to have the military presence of the countries concerned in a limited portion of the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for a limited period...as a stage in the implementation of the Lusaka Agreement.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Proposes a new, interim security arrangement to facilitate foreign troop withdrawal by addressing the security concerns of neighboring countries.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission reiterated the strong position of the Security Council that the city of Kisangani should be demilitarized immediately and without conditions.
records.political_signal: The Security Council's patience on the demilitarization of Kisangani is exhausted, and it demands immediate compliance with its resolutions.
records.policy_implication: Non-compliance could lead to further Council action.

records.record_text: Members of the Security Council mission expressed to their various interlocutors their deep concern over the serious violations of human rights and the appalling humanitarian situation of much of the population in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as a result of the conflict.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: The Council is monitoring the human rights and humanitarian situation, linking it directly to the conflict.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission proposed that new impetus be given to the consideration of an international conference on peace, security and development in the Great Lakes region that could be convened at an appropriate time.
records.political_signal: Signaling a long-term, comprehensive approach is needed to address the root causes of conflict in the region.
records.policy_implication: The Council may support a broader regional conference to consolidate peace once immediate conflicts are resolved.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission made clear its position that the Council would severely condemn any party that violated the ceasefire in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: There is a zero-tolerance policy for ceasefire violations.
records.policy_implication: Any party breaking the ceasefire will face direct condemnation and potential punitive measures from the Security Council.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission was gratified to note that all its interlocutors agreed that negotiations should continue among the Congolese parties with a view to reaching a more comprehensive and inclusive agreement.
records.political_signal: The mission successfully established a consensus on the need for continued, inclusive talks.
records.policy_implication: null

records.record_text: The Security Council mission notes that some progress has been made in the withdrawal of foreign forces from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It must also be noted, however, that, of all the original belligerents, only Namibia has withdrawn all its combat troops from the territory. The withdrawals of contingents by Angola, Uganda and Zimbabwe are partial, and need to be finally verified. Reported withdrawals by Rwanda have been verified neither by MONUC nor by the Joint Military Commission.
records.political_signal: The mission is publicly tracking compliance with withdrawal commitments and highlighting shortcomings.
records.policy_implication: Increased pressure will be applied for verified, complete withdrawals, particularly from Rwanda.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission commends MONUC for the progress achieved so far in the disarmament, demobilization and repatriation of the Rwandan combatants at Kamina.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: null

records.record_text: The mission further takes note of the agreement in principle by the Government of Rwanda to accept a delegation representing the Kamina combatants, and trusts that this important confidence-building measure can be accomplished at an early date.
records.political_signal: The mission is registering Rwanda's commitment and setting an expectation for its prompt fulfillment.
records.policy_implication: This measure is seen as a key CBM for the broader DDRRR process.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission takes note of the solemn reiteration by the RCD leadership before the Ministers of the Political Committee and the Ambassadors of the Security Council of their “irrevocable” commitment to demilitarizing Kisangani, and calls on them to proceed to take the necessary steps without further delay.
records.political_signal: The Council has put RCD-Goma on the record and will hold them to their 'irrevocable' commitment, demanding immediate action.
records.policy_implication: The credibility of RCD-Goma is at stake; failure to act will be seen as a direct defiance of the Security Council.

records.record_text: Evidence presented by representatives of women’s groups indicated how deeply the welfare and security of women and girls have been affected by the conflict.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Highlights the need for gender-specific considerations in humanitarian and human rights responses, as reflected in recommendation paragraph 28.

records.record_text: The mission heard from President Kagame that Rwanda would wish to work closely with such a united administration on the demobilization of the armed groups, and that Rwanda’s presence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was related only to its legitimate security concerns.
records.political_signal: Rwanda is linking its withdrawal to the formation of a unified DRC government capable of addressing its security concerns (i.e., armed groups).
records.policy_implication: This establishes a key conditionality from Rwanda's perspective for its withdrawal from DRC territory.

records.record_text: The mission made it clear that the Council would follow up on the next report of the Panel of Experts to the Security Council.
records.political_signal: The issue of illegal exploitation of resources is not being ignored and will remain on the Council's agenda, with potential for future action.
records.policy_implication: Parties involved in the illegal exploitation of resources are put on notice that the Council will review the Panel's findings and may act upon them.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council, within the next few days, should consider taking further initiatives on this matter in coordination with the signatories of the Lusaka Agreement and the leaders of the region.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Urges the Council to maintain momentum from the mission by taking immediate diplomatic action to help finalize an inclusive political agreement.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission recommends that the Council may wish, following the establishment of a fully inclusive Congolese transitional authority, to consider...adding to the future mandate of MONUC elements concerning the organization and conduct of free and fair elections.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Proposes a future expansion of MONUC's role to support the democratic transition, contingent on political progress.

records.record_text: The mission further recommends that the Secretary-General, if requested by the parties, could instruct MONUC to facilitate the development and implementation of the “curtain” proposal as an interim measure aimed at ensuring border security in the final stages of withdrawal.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Suggests a specific, operational role for MONUC in implementing the mission's new border security idea.

records.record_text: DDRRR in the east will pose serious problems of security. Further progress...will require the deployment of a robust force at Kindu within the existing mandate of MONUC.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Successful DDRRR in eastern DRC is contingent on a more robust MONUC presence, specifically a forward operating base in Kindu.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission recommends to the Security Council that it devote particular attention to the implementation of the MONUC mandate in the fields of human rights and humanitarian assistance to populations in need in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, taking fully into account the needs of women and girls.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Calls for strengthening MONUC's civilian components and ensuring a gender-sensitive approach to mandate implementation.

records.record_text: The Security Council should consider supporting the efforts of MONUC to train the Kisangani police force and taking prompt action on the request of the Secretary-General...for 85 additional police officers for this purpose.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Endorses the expansion of MONUC's police component to support security sector reform as part of the Kisangani demilitarization plan.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission takes the strong view that further progress in the peace process should take the form of economic dividends for the population. The delay in achieving this risks the credibility of the process and of the international community.
records.political_signal: The entire peace process is at risk if tangible improvements are not felt by the population.
records.policy_implication: Peacekeeping and political efforts must be accompanied by robust humanitarian and development aid to be sustainable.

records.record_text: It would be very useful if the regional leaders, in coordination with the United Nations, could ensure the establishment of a follow-up mechanism.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Proposes a new coordinating body to manage the multiple, complex tracks of the peace process, acknowledging the Council cannot do it alone.

records.record_text: However, none of this progress is irreversible, and further efforts will be necessary to ensure the success of the peace process in Burundi to achieve the cessation of hostilities and a ceasefire...
records.political_signal: Progress in Burundi is fragile and can be easily reversed without a comprehensive ceasefire.
records.policy_implication: The political gains of the Arusha Agreement are at risk as long as the fighting continues.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission demanded that the rebel groups cease hostilities immediately and enter into negotiations with the support of the facilitation within the framework of the Arusha Agreement.
records.political_signal: The mission issued a direct, non-negotiable demand to the armed groups, using the strongest possible diplomatic language.
records.policy_implication: This sets a clear benchmark for compliance by the rebel groups.

records.record_text: It is the view of the Security Council mission that, without an urgent cessation of hostilities, followed by a ceasefire agreement, the peace process could be jeopardized. It is also the view of most of the heads of State of the region, some of whom expressed doubts concerning the willingness of the armed groups to enter into negotiations. Some considered the time might have come to contemplate more robust measures. If that were the case, the possibility of regional sanctions has been raised.
records.political_signal: The mission is signaling that patience is wearing thin and that regional actors are considering punitive measures, including sanctions, against intransigent armed groups.
records.policy_implication: The Council may be asked to support or endorse regional enforcement actions if negotiations fail.

records.record_text: All the mission’s interlocutors, both Burundian and non-Burundian, stressed the risk that the tremendous economic and financial difficulties currently facing the country might undermine the peace process.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Economic collapse is a primary threat to the Burundi peace process, requiring urgent donor intervention.

records.record_text: The Council may also wish to encourage the States of the region to pursue their efforts to persuade the armed groups to agree to a cessation of hostilities and ceasefire agreement, and to extend full assistance to the facilitation in this regard.
records.political_signal: null
records.policy_implication: Recommends a strategy of leveraging regional influence to pressure Burundian armed groups.

records.record_text: The mission stresses the need for the implementation of reforms called for in the Arusha Agreement by the transitional Government and its institutions, with or without a ceasefire, to the full extent the military situation allows.
records.political_signal: Political reforms should not be held hostage by the lack of a ceasefire; progress must continue where possible.
records.policy_implication: The Council will assess the Transitional Government's performance based on its commitment to implementing Arusha reforms, not just on the security situation.

records.record_text: It will in particular be essential for donors to fulfil the commitments they made at the Paris conference of December 2000 and the Geneva conference of December 2001. The mission will follow up with the international financial institutions on this point. There is a risk that the peace process, and all the gains made with it so far, might collapse if further assistance, including direct aid, is not forthcoming in the near future.
records.political_signal: The mission is putting donors on notice that failure to disburse pledged funds could lead to the collapse of the entire peace process, and commits to an active follow-up role.
records.policy_implication: The mission identifies a direct link between donor funding and the survival of the peace process, creating a strong moral and political case for immediate disbursement.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Ethiopia and Eritrea

main_risks: Potential for unilateral, destabilizing actions by either party following the Boundary Commission's decision.
Incomplete cooperation on freedom of movement for UNMEE, particularly from Eritrea.
Delays in demining, which is a prerequisite for physical border demarcation.
Lack of direct flights for UNMEE between Asmara and Addis Ababa, impeding operations and increasing costs.
Failure to release all prisoners of war and civilian detainees.
main_commitments: The Security Council will prepare a resolution to renew UNMEE's mandate and provide a framework for the implementation of the Boundary Commission's decision.
The Security Council is committed to assisting the parties in implementing the delimitation decision.
The Secretary-General will be requested to submit recommendations on the demarcation process.
main_policy_signals: The international community attaches 'monumental importance' to the parties' full acceptance of the final and binding Boundary Commission decision.
The existing security arrangements, including the Temporary Security Zone (TSZ), must remain in effect until demarcation is complete.
The transfer of territory and civilian authority must be orderly and without unilateral actions.
The Security Council provides its unwavering support to UNMEE and the peace process.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Ethiopia and Eritrea was a high-level political engagement conducted at a critical juncture just before the Boundary Commission's border delimitation ruling. Its primary purpose was to reinforce the final and binding nature of the upcoming decision, urge both parties to cooperate in its implementation, and assess the requirements for UNMEE's mandate renewal. The mission successfully engaged with the leaders of Ethiopia and Eritrea, securing their public reaffirmation of commitment to the Algiers Agreements. It also assessed the security and humanitarian situation on the ground, including in the Temporary Security Zone, and consulted a wide range of national and international stakeholders. The report outlines a clear sequence of recommendations for the Council, focusing on an orderly, UN-facilitated demarcation process, demining, confidence-building measures, and continued international support, while clearly signaling the major risk of unilateral actions post-decision.

activities.activity_description: Meeting with Prime Minister of Ethiopia, Meles Zenawi, in Addis Ababa.
Meeting with the President of Eritrea, Isaias Afwerki, in Asmara.
Meeting with the Secretary-General of the Organization of African Unity (OAU), Amara Essy, in Addis Ababa.
Meeting with representatives of the United Nations Mission in Ethiopia and Eritrea (UNMEE) and of troop-contributing countries.
Meetings with the diplomatic community in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Meetings with the United Nations country teams in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Meetings with religious leaders in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Meetings with non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in Addis Ababa and Asmara.
Ceremonial crossing from Ethiopia to Eritrea at the Mereb River Bridge.
Visit to the Temporary Security Zone.
Briefing by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and the Force Commander on the situation in the mission area.

activities.activity_type: Visit to Community or Project Site
activities.activity_description: Visit to the town of Senafe, including the Mine Risk Education Project.

activities.activity_type: Visit to Community or Project Site
activities.activity_description: Visit to a camp of some 5,000 internally displaced persons near Senafe.
Operational briefing on the situation in the central sector of the Temporary Security Zone at the Indian Battalion’s base at Camp Dunn.
Press conference by the Chairperson of the Security Council mission.
Wrap-up meeting with the Special Representative of the Secretary-General.

actors_met.actor_name: Meles Zenawi, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
Amara Essy, Secretary-General of the Organization of African Unity
United Nations Mission in Ethiopia and Eritrea (UNMEE)
Legwaila Joseph Legwaila, Special Representative of the Secretary-General

records.record_text: The mission welcomed recent statements by both sides, reaffirming that the decision by the Boundary Commission is final and binding.
records.political_signal: The mission notes and reinforces the parties' public commitments to the final and binding nature of the Boundary Commission decision.

records.record_text: The international community attaches the highest importance to this decision and praises the resolution by peaceful means of the border conflict. The commitments of both parties in this regard represent a pivotal measure of their dedication to the peace process.
records.political_signal: Acceptance of the Boundary Commission's decision is presented as the ultimate test of the parties' commitment to peace.

records.record_text: The mission assured the parties that the Security Council is strongly committed to doing its part to assist them in the implementation of the delimitation decision.
records.political_signal: The Security Council signals its intent to remain actively engaged and provide tangible support during the demarcation phase.
records.policy_implication: Foreshadows a future Council resolution providing a framework and potential resources for the implementation phase.

records.record_text: UNMEE’s contribution, in cooperation with both parties, towards improving the situation of the people, especially in the Temporary Security Zone, are strongly commended by the mission.
records.political_signal: Strong expression of support and validation for UNMEE's work on the ground.

records.record_text: In the crucial period ahead, it will be particularly important that the Special Representative of the Secretary-General has easy accessibility to both sides in order to discuss the further steps to be taken.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the central role of the SRSG as the primary channel for dialogue and problem-solving during the implementation phase.

records.record_text: In order to enhance popular understanding of UNMEE’s role, especially among those living in the Temporary Security Zone, the mission also encouraged the leaders to make arrangements for UNMEE radio broadcasts.
The mission noted with satisfaction that the situation on the ground, and inside the Temporary Security Zone in particular, remains calm.
records.policy_implication: Affirms the effectiveness of the TSZ and the parties' general adherence to the ceasefire.

records.record_text: The mission underlined its expectation that all necessary steps for the implementation of the Boundary Commission’s delimitation determination will commence immediately following the Commission’s announcement, which is expected in the latter part of March 2002.
records.political_signal: The Council is signaling that it expects no delays from the parties in moving from the legal decision to the practical implementation phase.

records.record_text: The mission urged the parties to extend their full cooperation to UNMEE in its efforts to reach a common understanding on effective modalities and procedures for the implementation phase.

The mission informed the leaders of its expectation that the Security Council will prepare a resolution in support of the process. That resolution, scheduled for consideration in mid-March 2002, would renew the mandate of UNMEE and provide an overall framework for the implementation phase.
records.political_signal: The Council is providing advance notice of its intended formal action to support the post-decision phase.
records.policy_implication: Signals the Council's intent to adjust UNMEE's mandate to include specific implementation and demarcation support tasks.

records.record_text: This could be done through appropriate strengthening of the Military Coordination Commission, for example, by establishing sector-level committees. In addition, a more wide-ranging mechanism aimed at implementation-related consultation and problem-solving should probably be considered.
records.policy_implication: Proposes specific institutional adjustments to manage the complexities of the demarcation and implementation phase.

records.record_text: The mission recalled that, in accordance with article 14 of the Agreement on Cessation of Hostilities (S/2000/601, annex), the security arrangements are to remain in effect. Accordingly, arrangements for the separation of the forces, as achieved by the establishment of the Temporary Security Zone, will continue to be of key importance. Until the border demarcation has been completed, UNMEE will continue to discharge its mandate.
records.political_signal: The Council is unequivocally stating that the Boundary Commission's decision does not automatically terminate the TSZ or UNMEE's mandate; these will continue until physical demarcation is complete.
records.policy_implication: This clarifies the legal and operational basis for UNMEE's continued presence and activities post-decision.

records.record_text: The mission further emphasized that transfer of territory and civil authority should take place in an orderly manner, without any unilateral actions.
records.political_signal: A direct warning against any pre-emptive or uncoordinated moves by either party in areas affected by the border decision.

records.record_text: ...the parties requested the United Nations to facilitate resolution of problems that may arise due to the transfer of territorial control, including the consequences for individuals residing in previously disputed territory.
records.policy_implication: Reaffirms the mandate basis (from the Algiers Agreement) for the UN to play a role in addressing the human dimension of border demarcation.

records.record_text: The mission urged the parties to refrain from any actions that could have destabilizing effects, including population movements and movements of troops and militia, until modalities and procedures are agreed upon.
records.political_signal: The Council identifies uncontrolled population and troop movements as a primary threat to stability following the decision.
records.policy_implication: This warning establishes a benchmark for judging the parties' conduct in the implementation phase.

records.record_text: The mission emphasized that demining is an essential prerequisite to border demarcation.
records.policy_implication: Establishes demining as a critical path item for the entire demarcation process, implying that lack of progress on demining will halt demarcation.

records.record_text: The mission strongly urged both parties to release and return all prisoners of war and civilian detainees at the earliest opportunity under the auspices of the International Committee of the Red Cross in accordance with the Geneva Conventions and the Algiers Agreements.
records.political_signal: The Council highlights the release of PoWs and detainees as a key outstanding obligation and confidence-building measure.

records.record_text: The mission ... expresses the expectation that, notwithstanding those arrangements, full freedom of movement will be provided for UNMEE to monitor the redeployed forces of Eritrea, to disclose the number, strength and disposition of its militia and police inside the Temporary Security Zone and to conclude the status-of-forces agreement with the Secretary-General.
records.political_signal: The Council formally notes its dissatisfaction with existing restrictions and lists specific, unresolved issues with Eritrea.
records.policy_implication: Continued non-compliance could become a significant issue in future mandate renewals.

records.record_text: The mission expresses its disappointment at the continuing failure by the parties to establish a direct high-altitude flight route for UNMEE between Addis Ababa and Asmara.
records.political_signal: The Council is publicly expressing frustration over an issue that signals a lack of full cooperation and has direct financial and operational consequences for the UN.

records.record_text: The Secretary-General should be invited to submit recommendations at an early stage, taking into account the decision of the Boundary Commission, the contributions of the parties, the capacity of UNMEE and the resources available in the United Nations Trust Fund in Support of the Delimitation and Demarcation of the Ethiopia/Eritrea Border.
records.policy_implication: This recommendation formally tasks the Secretariat with developing a concrete operational plan for the UN's role in demarcation, which will form the basis for a subsequent Security Council decision.

records.record_text: In the light of the above and other relevant recommendations, the Security Council should consider how UNMEE can play an appropriate role in the demarcation process;
records.policy_implication: This self-directed recommendation initiates the Council's own deliberation process on adjusting UNMEE's mandate for the demarcation phase.

records.record_text: The mission appeals to the guarantors, the facilitators and the witnesses of the peace process, OAU and the friends of Eritrea and Ethiopia to continue to intensify their contacts with the authorities of both countries, in order to promote a constructive dialogue with the aim of opening a new page in the history of their relations;
records.political_signal: The Council is calling for a broad, coordinated diplomatic effort to support the peace process beyond the UN's direct role.

records.record_text: The mission therefore encourages urgent contributions to the Consolidated Appeals process for 2002 in both countries in order to face the challenges that lie ahead. The Security Council strongly appeals to donors to be generous;
records.political_signal: The Security Council is using its political weight to advocate for humanitarian funding.

records.record_text: The mission accordingly hopes the Secretary-General will take action to appoint a new Deputy Special Representative in Asmara soon;
records.political_signal: The mission is flagging a key leadership vacancy that needs to be filled to ensure UNMEE is at full operational capacity for the crucial period ahead.

records.record_text: ...the mission would strongly encourage the parties to continue to search for mutually agreeable ways of building trust through increased official as well as grass-roots contact with each other, with a view to moving towards political and economic cooperation.
records.political_signal: The Council is looking beyond the narrow border issue to the long-term goal of normalized relations and cooperation.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission on the implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999)

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: UN Mission Oversight, Situation Assessment, Political Engagement
main_risks: Breakdown of the political process due to non-participation of the Kosovo Serb community.
Ongoing inter-ethnic violence, extremism, and lack of trust hindering reconciliation.
Inadequate security for minority communities, which impedes the return of refugees and IDPs.
Regional instability, particularly along the border with the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
main_commitments: The Mission committed to raising the issues of returns, detainees, and missing persons with FRY President Kostunica.
KFOR undertook to provide the Security Council Committee 1160 with detailed information on seized weapons.
main_policy_signals: Insistence on the participation of all communities, especially Kosovo Serbs, in the upcoming Kosovo-wide elections.
Strong and unequivocal rejection of violence, extremism, and terrorism directed at all community leaders.
Call for the Kosovo Albanian leadership to improve the treatment and respect for the rights of minority communities.
Reinforcement of UNMIK's authority and the political process as defined by UNSCR 1244 (1999).
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: This three-day Security Council mission to Kosovo and Belgrade, the first comprising all 15 members, was a hybrid political, oversight, and assessment engagement. The mission concluded that while UNMIK had made considerable progress in implementing UNSCR 1244, it was at a critical juncture requiring sustained international support. Through high-level engagement with a diverse range of actors, the mission strongly endorsed the political process centered on the new Constitutional Framework and upcoming elections, framing it as essential to combating extremism. The core message delivered was a call for all communities, particularly Kosovo Serbs, to participate in the political process, while simultaneously urging the Kosovo Albanian leadership to improve security and rights for minorities. The mission identified inter-ethnic distrust, poor security for minorities, and the unresolved issue of missing persons as primary obstacles to a multi-ethnic Kosovo, and it explicitly recommended increased resources for justice and policing, as well as continued dialogue with Belgrade.

activities.activity_description: Received a comprehensive briefing by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, as well as briefings by the Principal Deputy Special Representative and Deputy Special Representatives of UNMIK’s Pillars.
Met with representatives of the Kosovo Albanian families of the missing and detained, who delivered a petition.
A representative group of Kosovo women’s NGOs met with members of the Mission.
Met the President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Committee on Kosovo, Mr. Momcilo Trajkovic, and other members of the committee.
Met the United Nations Regional Administration in Mitrovica.
Met separately with Kosovo Albanian and Kosovo Serb representatives in Mitrovica.
Attended a special session of the Interim Administrative Council, which included selected members of the Kosovo Transitional Council.
Met with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who was visiting the region.
Was briefed by the new KFOR Commander, Lieutenant General Thorstein Skiaker, on the security situation at KFOR Headquarters.
The Mission and the Special Representative held a joint press conference at Pristina.
Had meetings in Belgrade with the President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Vojislav Kostunica, Foreign Minister Svilanovic and Interior Minister Zivkovic.

actors_met.actor_name: Hans Haekkerup, Special Representative of the Secretary-General
UNMIK Principal Deputy Special Representative and Deputy Special Representatives
Representatives of the Kosovo Albanian families of the missing and detained
Momcilo Trajkovic, President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Committee on Kosovo
Dusan Celic, Deputy President of the FRY Committee on Kosovo
Alekesandr Simic, Kosovo Serb representative in the Joint Working Group on the Constitutional Framework
United Nations Regional Administration in Mitrovica
Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation
Lieutenant General Thorstein Skiaker, KFOR Commander
Vojislav Kostunica, President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

records.record_text: UNMIK believed that the next six months would be decisive for the future of a multi-ethnic Kosovo.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the urgency of the political process and the need for immediate progress on inter-ethnic relations.

records.record_text: The security situation for Kosovo’s minority communities remained of great concern.
records.policy_implication: Indicates that security for minorities is a fundamental problem that undermines other efforts like returns and political participation.

records.record_text: The Committee on Kosovo underscored that the establishment of the committee was a demonstrable act by the Government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia aimed at conveying to the international community its keen interest in being a constructive facilitator in the implementation of Security Council resolution 1244 (1999).
records.political_signal: FRY government is positioning itself as a cooperative and constructive partner in the Kosovo process.

records.record_text: They underscored that the Constitutional Framework in its present form was unacceptable and, as they saw it, excluded all non-Albanians from the political process. Furthermore, they considered that the inclusion of the judiciary and Presidency provisions in the Constitutional Framework had set the basis for Kosovo’s independence.
records.political_signal: Signaling deep opposition to the Constitutional Framework, viewing it as a vehicle for independence and exclusion of Serbs.
records.policy_implication: Indicates a major political obstacle to Kosovo Serb participation in the UNMIK-led process and elections.

records.record_text: The Mission delivered a firm message on the importance of Kosovo Serb participation and integration into the political process.
records.political_signal: The Security Council's primary political objective is to secure Kosovo Serb participation in the established political structures.

records.record_text: It was clear from the presentation of both parties, however, that dispelling the continuing climate of mutual distrust remained a major challenge for inter-communal activities and attempts at reconciliation.
records.policy_implication: Deep-seated mistrust is the root cause of the division in Mitrovica and a fundamental barrier to progress.

records.record_text: He stressed the need for the international community to work together more closely, noting that only through joint action and a united approach could resolution 1244 (1999) be successfully implemented.
records.actor_source: Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation
records.political_signal: A call for unity within the international community, possibly implying criticism of unilateral or uncoordinated actions.

records.record_text: General Skiaker noted that KFOR operations continued to result in frequent weapons seizures during its border monitoring. Upon further clarification with regard to the requirements of the Committee, he undertook to provide the Committee with the requested information in the future.
records.actor_target: Security Council Committee established pursuant to resolution 1160 (1998)
records.policy_implication: Establishes a new reporting mechanism from KFOR to a Security Council sanctions committee.

records.record_text: UNMIK has made considerable progress in implementing Security Council resolution 1244 (1999) in the two years since its establishment, although there remains a lot to be done.

UNMIK has now reached a critical stage in the implementation of its mandate and continued effectiveness requires a major effort by UNMIK, KFOR and UNMIK Police, backed up by close attention from the Security Council and the sustained input of resources from the international community.
records.political_signal: The mission's success is at a tipping point and failure is a real possibility without increased support and resources.
records.policy_implication: A failure to provide additional resources and political backing could jeopardize the entire mission.

records.record_text: The Mission underlined that elections will enhance the democratic process in Kosovo and the stability of the region and stressed that secure conditions for the elections should be ensured.
records.political_signal: The Security Council fully endorses the holding of elections as the path forward.
records.policy_implication: Commits the international presence (UNMIK/KFOR) to ensuring a secure electoral environment.

records.record_text: Current obstacles include inadequate physical, social and economic security for the communities in particular, alongside a lack of freedom of movement and equal access to public services.
records.policy_implication: These are the core issues that must be addressed to enable a multi-ethnic society and successful political process.

records.record_text: In recognition of the need to improve security and law enforcement, the Mission welcomes the establishment by the Special Representative of Pillar I and key legislation to combat organized crime, illegal weapons possession and terrorism.

It notes the need for additional resources in the key areas of justice and policing and the need to create a new Assistant Secretary-General (ASG) position to head Pillar I. It underlined the need to provide an increased number of international judges and prosecutors and funding for additional detention facilities.
records.policy_implication: The mission formally endorses a significant increase in international resources and personnel for the justice and security sector.

records.record_text: The Mission recommends that a formal request be sent to KFOR to regularly provide detailed information including that pertaining to the origin, type and quantity of weapons seized, in order to enable the Security Council Committee established pursuant to resolution 1160 (1998) to pursue any possible violations.
records.policy_implication: Formalizes and strengthens the monitoring of the arms embargo by linking KFOR's operational findings directly to a Security Council body.

records.record_text: The Mission recommends that more intensified efforts should be put into the issue of the missing of all communities and detainees, which continues to be a major impediment to reconciliation and was an issue raised by almost every Kosovo representative the Mission met.
records.policy_implication: Elevates the issue of missing persons to a top priority for reconciliation, requiring greater effort from the international mission.

records.record_text: Recognizing that the continued division is based on fear and mutual distrust, and that there is a necessity for a careful approach, the Mission places emphasis on the need for multi-ethnic initiatives in the social, economic and religious areas to start rebuilding confidence between the communities.
records.policy_implication: Advocates for a 'soft power' approach in Mitrovica, focusing on grassroots confidence-building rather than solely security measures.

records.record_text: The Mission conveyed firm and balanced messages to all community leaders that the responsibility lies with them to clearly and openly reject violence, extremism and terrorism.
records.political_signal: Places direct responsibility on local leaders for curbing extremism and violence.

records.record_text: The Mission’s strong message to the Kosovo Albanian leadership was the need to be more forthcoming with regard to improving the treatment of the minority communities.
records.political_signal: The majority community has a special responsibility to protect and improve conditions for minorities.

records.record_text: The Kosovo Serb community, in particular, must integrate into the structures being set up by UNMIK, rather than attempt to set up parallel structures.
records.political_signal: There is no alternative to participation in the UNMIK-led process; parallel structures are unacceptable.
records.policy_implication: Signals non-recognition and likely future dismantling of any Serb-run parallel institutions.

records.record_text: The Mission believes that UNMIK must continue and enhance its dialogue with the authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, whose influence in Kosovo is key on the implementation of resolution 1244 (1999).
records.policy_implication: Endorses the strategy of engaging Belgrade as a necessary component for achieving mission objectives inside Kosovo.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region, 15-26 May 2001

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Implementation Review, Political Engagement, Situation Assessment
main_risks: Loss of momentum in the DRC peace process due to non-compliance or subjective interpretation of agreements by parties.
Failure of parties to provide detailed operational plans for withdrawal and DDR, which would prevent the UN from planning and executing MONUC Phase III.
The potential for the Burundi conflict to escalate into a wider regional crisis, fueled by movements of armed groups from the DRC and the impasse in the Arusha process.
Non-compliance by RCD with the demand to demilitarize Kisangani, undermining the authority of the Security Council and the peace process.
Continued illegitimate exploitation of DRC's natural resources creating spoilers and prolonging the conflict.
main_commitments: The Political Committee adopted draft plans for the total withdrawal of foreign forces and for the DDR of armed groups.
The neutral facilitator, Sir Ketumile Masire, announced the convening of a preparatory meeting for the inter-Congolese dialogue on 16 July.
FLC leader Jean-Pierre Bemba committed to disengaging his forces by 1 June.
The Security Council mission committed to recommending the transition to MONUC Phase III, conditional on party cooperation.
Uganda committed to establishing a commission of inquiry into the allegations made by the Panel of Experts on illegal exploitation.
main_policy_signals: The Lusaka and Arusha Agreements are the sole frameworks for peace in the DRC and Burundi respectively, and are not subject to revision.
All foreign forces, regardless of whether they were 'invited' or 'uninvited', must withdraw from the DRC.
The DDR of armed groups is the key to ending the conflict in the DRC, and progress is directly linked to the withdrawal of Rwandan forces.
There is no military solution to the conflict in Burundi; parties who continue to use force will face international rejection.
The Security Council is resolute in enforcing its resolutions, particularly the demilitarization of Kisangani, and will not tolerate defiance.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission capitalized on a perceived 'window of opportunity' in the DRC peace process following the accession of President Joseph Kabila. Through extensive high-level diplomacy across eight countries, the mission successfully advanced the Lusaka process by securing renewed commitments, draft plans for withdrawal and DDR, and a date for the inter-Congolese dialogue. It simultaneously addressed the intractable Burundian conflict, delivering a strong, unified message against military options and in support of the Arusha framework. The mission found the DRC situation 'encouraging' but fragile, contingent on party compliance, while the Burundi situation was assessed as 'complex and intractable' with a high risk of escalation. The report recommends a conditional move to MONUC Phase III and enhanced support for the Burundi peace process, clearly linking international support to tangible progress and compliance by the parties on the ground.

Rassemblement congolais pour la démocratie (RCD Goma)

records.record_text: Members of the mission stressed the need to ensure that progress in the political sphere of the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement, notably the dialogue, was made in parallel with the military aspects, namely, the withdrawal of foreign forces and the disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation or resettlement of armed groups.
records.political_signal: The mission insists on the principle of parallel progress on both political and military tracks of the Lusaka Agreement.
records.policy_implication: The Council will likely condition its support for one track (e.g., military withdrawal) on tangible progress in the other (inter-Congolese dialogue).

records.record_text: Mr. Mandela advised the Security Council mission to make it very clear to the armed groups that there was no military solution, and that dialogue was the sole means of reaching agreement.

In his response, President Kabila placed great emphasis on his Government’s view that the Rwandan and Ugandan troops in the Democratic Republic of the Congo were forces of aggression — not “uninvited forces” — and that, in accordance with resolution 1304 (2000), they should withdraw forthwith.
records.political_signal: DRC Government rejects the moral equivalency between its allies and Rwandan/Ugandan forces, framing the latter as aggressors who must withdraw unconditionally.
records.policy_implication: This position complicates negotiations on a sequenced and reciprocal withdrawal of all foreign forces as envisioned by the Lusaka Agreement.

records.record_text: The mission stressed that the establishment and maintenance of productive bilateral channels between Kinshasa and Kigali were vital to the restoration of peace and the development of democracy and prosperity in the subregion. This was the key to the disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation or resettlement of armed groups, since the United Nations would not be in a position to track them down and disarm them by force.
records.political_signal: The mission clearly states that bilateral cooperation between DRC and Rwanda is a prerequisite for a successful DDR process, which the UN cannot enforce militarily.
records.policy_implication: The success of the UN's role in DDR is explicitly tied to the political will and direct cooperation of the concerned states, particularly DRC and Rwanda.

records.record_text: President Mugabe said that Zimbabwean troops would withdraw in accordance with the same principles that had required their original deployment, and after their original goals had been met. It would also be necessary to ensure, perhaps through the institution of mechanisms under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations, that there was no risk of the return of Ugandan, Rwandan and Burundian troops.
records.political_signal: Zimbabwe conditions its withdrawal on the complete and guaranteed departure of opposing forces, suggesting a need for a robust Chapter VII enforcement mechanism.
records.policy_implication: This stance introduces a sequentiality ('invaders must go first') that contradicts the Lusaka principle of a coordinated withdrawal of all foreign forces.

records.record_text: All members of the mission then presented to the FDD leader a very clear and strong message: there was no prospect of military victory in the Burundi conflict; the only way to resolve it was through peaceful negotiations; any party which came to power through the use of force could expect nothing but rejection from the international community; while, by contrast, all those who engaged in negotiations towards a peaceful settlement could expect international support...
records.political_signal: The mission delivered a clear 'carrots and sticks' message: engage in peaceful negotiation for international support or face international isolation if military force is used to seize power.
records.policy_implication: The Security Council is establishing a clear norm against the forceful takeover of government in Burundi and setting the terms for legitimate international engagement.

records.record_text: It was agreed that all foreign forces should leave the Democratic Republic of the Congo, whether invited or not.
records.political_signal: The mission asserts its position, overriding the distinction made by some parties between 'invited' and 'uninvited' forces.
records.policy_implication: This principle forms the basis for the Council's demand for a comprehensive withdrawal of all foreign armies, undermining the legal justification used by DRC's allies.

records.record_text: Members of the Security Council mission insisted that the parties should provide the necessary detailed information concerning the numbers, locations, assembly areas, withdrawal routes and timetables in order to allow the United Nations to make its own plans to assist the parties and to monitor the process.
records.policy_implication: UN assistance for withdrawal and DDR (Phase III) is contingent on the parties providing actionable operational data.

records.record_text: Members stressed that it was necessary to advance the peace process step by step. The disengagement plan and the ceasefire should be strictly observed, and parties responsible for violations should bear the consequences.
records.political_signal: The mission signals that there will be accountability for ceasefire violations and non-compliance with agreed plans.
records.policy_implication: The Council is putting parties on notice that it may consider targeted measures against violators to protect the integrity of the peace process.

records.record_text: Members of the mission then raised the matter of the demilitarization of Kisangani, pursuant to Security Council resolution 1304 (2000). Although Rwanda and Uganda had both withdrawn their troops from the city in compliance with that resolution, RCD remained there in force... The RCD forces must withdraw from Kisangani.
records.political_signal: The mission is adamant about the full implementation of Resolution 1304, specifically targeting RCD's continued presence.
records.policy_implication: Failure by RCD to comply constitutes a direct challenge to the Security Council's authority and could trigger further Council action.

records.record_text: The Secretary-General of RCD, Azarias Ruberwa, strongly objected to this demand. RCD had not been named in resolution 1304 (2000), and in any case the Security Council had no right to order Congolese to withdraw from Congolese territory.
records.political_signal: RCD challenges the legal authority and interpretation of the Security Council's resolution, using a sovereignty argument to justify its non-compliance.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission warned RCD not to mistake the strength of purpose of the Security Council, which maintained its insistence on the implementation of its resolutions through all difficulties and delays. It would be better for RCD to respond to the Security Council’s demand with reflection rather than defiance. ... They must comply.
records.political_signal: The mission delivered a direct and unambiguous threat to RCD, asserting the Council's resolve and demanding compliance with its resolutions.
records.policy_implication: This sets up a direct confrontation between the Council and RCD, where non-compliance would likely lead to punitive measures or a loss of legitimacy for RCD.

records.record_text: The Minister said the implementation of the Lusaka Agreement was having a negative impact on Burundi, and that Lusaka could pose even more serious problems for Burundi in the future if it were not implemented completely, including with the disarmament of the armed groups. Burundian rebels, ex-FAR, Interahamwe and other groups were now moving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo into Burundi.
records.policy_implication: The DRC peace process is creating a 'spillover' effect, destabilizing Burundi by pushing armed groups across the border, creating a linkage that policy-makers must address.

records.record_text: President Buyoya said the armed groups had chosen the military option, and must be persuaded to negotiate. If the rebels refused, then the region should impose sanctions against them, as promised at the Nairobi summit in September 2000.

President Mkapa expressed concern at what he called the growing tendency to criticize the “aggressors” of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and to belittle the potential dangers of the armed groups for the security of Rwanda, Uganda and possibly Burundi.
records.political_signal: Tanzania warns against a simplistic narrative of the DRC conflict that ignores the legitimate security concerns of neighboring states, which could undermine a durable peace.

records.record_text: Ministers made it clear that the Government of Rwanda insisted on the full disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation or resettlement of armed groups and substantial progress in the inter-Congolese dialogue before withdrawing their forces from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.political_signal: Rwanda establishes clear and substantial conditions for its withdrawal, linking its military presence directly to the resolution of the armed groups issue and political progress in DRC.
records.policy_implication: This sequencing (DDR and ICD progress first, then withdrawal) contrasts with calls for immediate withdrawal and creates a major point of negotiation and potential deadlock.

records.record_text: President Kagame identified three elements of the next phase of the peace process in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation or resettlement of armed groups, the inter-Congolese dialogue, and the withdrawal of foreign forces, in that order.
records.political_signal: President Kagame explicitly outlines a sequential approach to the peace process, placing withdrawal of forces as the final step after DDR and ICD.
records.policy_implication: This represents a significant conceptual disagreement with the principle of parallel implementation and unconditional withdrawal of all foreign forces.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission assured President Kagame that the Security Council attached the greatest importance to the security of Rwanda. There could be no peace in the Great Lakes region unless there was peace in Rwanda.
records.political_signal: The mission acknowledges the legitimacy of Rwanda's security concerns and frames Rwandan security as central to regional stability.
records.policy_implication: This message is intended to build trust with Kigali and indicates the Council's willingness to address the root causes of Rwanda's intervention (the armed groups) as part of a comprehensive solution.

records.record_text: Expressing their concern, the members of the mission said the Council would react sharply if FLC did not disengage to the agreed position as from 1 June, as stipulated in the joint communiqué adopted by the Security Council and the Political Committee.
records.political_signal: The mission issues a direct warning to FLC, threatening a 'sharp reaction' for non-compliance with the agreed disengagement timeline.
records.policy_implication: The Council is demonstrating its resolve to enforce military disengagement plans and will hold parties accountable for specific, time-bound commitments.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission found much that was encouraging in its visit to the Great Lakes region. For the first time since the outbreak of the conflict, the outlines of a solution appeared to be taking shape.
records.policy_implication: This positive assessment justifies the mission's key recommendation to seize the 'window of opportunity' and proceed with expanded UN engagement.

records.record_text: The mission recommends that the Security Council be prepared to consider, on the basis of specific recommendations to be submitted by the Secretary-General in his forthcoming report, approving a transition to phase III of the activities of MONUC.
records.policy_implication: This is the central operational recommendation for the DRC, paving the way for MONUC's expansion to assist with withdrawal and DDR, a significant deepening of UN involvement.

records.record_text: The mission invites the Security Council to consider further measures to promote compliance with resolution 1304 (2000), perhaps on the recommendation of the Secretary-General.
records.policy_implication: The mission is signaling that if RCD does not comply with the demand to demilitarize Kisangani, the Council should be prepared to take punitive action.

records.record_text: The disarmament, demobilization, reintegration and repatriation or resettlement of armed groups is the key to ending the conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
records.policy_implication: This assessment frames DDR as the central pillar of the peace strategy, implying it should be the main effort for the UN and the parties.

records.record_text: The mission welcomes indications that some foreign contingents have already been withdrawn, and recommends that the Security Council continue to urge all Governments with foreign forces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to withdraw them in a phased and reciprocal process, and in accordance with their undertakings in the Lusaka Agreement and the relevant resolutions of the Security Council.
The restoration of river traffic will permit the re-establishment of links between Kinshasa, Mbandaka and Kisangani, provided all parties cooperate.
records.political_signal: The reopening of the river is presented as a tangible peace dividend that can foster economic activity and national unity.
records.policy_implication: This highlights the importance of MONUC's role in peacebuilding activities beyond traditional peacekeeping, such as enabling economic recovery.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission recommends that, if no progress is made within three months, the Council consider taking the measures necessary to put an end to any continuing illegitimate exploitation.
records.policy_implication: The mission sets a deadline for action against the illegal exploitation of resources, raising the prospect of sanctions or other punitive measures if parties do not cooperate with the Panel of Experts.

records.record_text: The mission was struck by the complexity and intractability of the situation in Burundi, and its serious potential for large-scale violence.
records.policy_implication: This assessment provides a stark contrast to the cautious optimism regarding the DRC, flagging Burundi as a high-risk area requiring urgent attention.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission delivered a very strong message to all its Burundian interlocutors: there is no military solution to the conflict; peace can be achieved only through negotiations within the framework of the Arusha Agreement; all parties must be prepared to compromise.
records.political_signal: The mission firmly establishes the Arusha Agreement as the only legitimate path to peace and rules out any alternative, particularly a military one.

records.record_text: It is clear to the Security Council mission that no action that damages Burundi can truly assist the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Security Council will continue to support a global solution that can assist in restoring peace to both countries, and to the entire Great Lakes region.
records.political_signal: The mission articulates a core finding that the conflicts in the DRC and Burundi are interlinked and require a holistic, regional approach rather than separate solutions.
records.policy_implication: Future UN strategy must address the cross-border dynamics of the conflicts, particularly the movement of armed groups, to be effective.

records.record_text: The Council may wish to invite recommendations from the Secretary-General for the strengthening of the office of the facilitator, and for broadening the role of the Representative of the Secretary-General.
records.policy_implication: The mission identifies a need to bolster the UN's political and mediation capacity in Burundi to break the deadlock in the Arusha process.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council Mission to East Timor and Indonesia

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Implementation Review and Political Engagement
main_risks: Continued militia activity, intimidation, and misinformation in West Timor refugee camps, preventing safe and voluntary returns.
The slow pace of the Indonesian justice process for the 1999 atrocities and the murder of UNHCR staff, risking a culture of impunity.
A severely under-resourced and underdeveloped justice system in East Timor, impeding the rule of law and reconciliation.
The potential for the refugee crisis and militia presence in West Timor to remain a source of instability for the entire island.
main_commitments: The Government of Indonesia committed to resolving the refugee issue, working with the UN on residual transitional issues, and reporting to the Security Council on its plans to eradicate intimidation in refugee camps.
The Indonesian Attorney-General committed to beginning trials for 1999 atrocities in early 2001 and to working with OHCHR.

The Security Council Mission committed to supporting UNTAET, advocating for post-independence assistance for East Timor, and encouraging a swift security assessment in West Timor to facilitate the return of humanitarian agencies.
main_policy_signals: The results of the Popular Consultation are non-negotiable and must be accepted by all parties, including refugees and pro-integration groups.
There will be no impunity for serious crimes; the international community expects swift and credible justice in both Indonesia and East Timor.
The return of international humanitarian agencies to West Timor is conditional on guaranteed security, which includes the disarmament and disbandment of militias.
The international community is prepared to support East Timor after independence, but this requires concurrent planning and commitment.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: A hybrid implementation review and political engagement mission that assessed progress and challenges in East Timor's transition under UNTAET and Indonesia's implementation of resolution 1319. The Mission observed significant progress in East Timor but identified critical gaps in the justice sector and reconstruction. In Indonesia, the Mission expressed high concern over the refugee crisis, continued militia intimidation in West Timor, and the slow pace of justice for the 1999 atrocities and UNHCR murders. The Mission combined direct field observation with high-level political dialogue, delivering firm political messages on accountability and the necessity for Indonesia to take decisive action, while also encouraging bilateral cooperation and planning for East Timor's future.

activities.activity_description: Prior to departure, met informally with representatives of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and of Member States contributing military or civilian police personnel to the United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor (UNTAET).
Prior to departure, met with Mr. Jose Ramos-Horta, the East Timorese cabinet member for foreign affairs.

In East Timor, held extensive discussions with the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Transitional Administrator for East Timor, Mr. Sergio Vieira de Mello, and senior civilian and military personnel in UNTAET.
In East Timor, held discussions with the Cabinet of the East Timor Transitional Administration.
In East Timor, held discussions with the Armed Forces for the National Liberation of East Timor (FALINTIL) Commander.
In East Timor, met with ten diplomatic offices (Australia, Brazil, China, Indonesia, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Portugal, the United Kingdom and the United States).
In East Timor, met with East Timorese non-governmental organizations, as well as leading figures in East Timor, namely, Xanana Gusmao, Jose Ramos-Horta and Mario Carrascalao.
In Dili, the Mission visited the site of the Santa Cruz massacre and laid wreaths to mark the ninth anniversary of the killings.
Visited the district of Suai in Sector West.
In Suai, received extensive briefings by UNTAET civilian and military personnel.
In Suai, met with representatives of the community.

activities.activity_type: Visit to Community or Project Site
activities.activity_description: In Suai, visited the site of the 1999 Suai church massacre, and a hospital rehabilitation project.

In Kupang, met and had extensive discussions with the Governor of East Nusa Tenggara, Piet Tallo, the Udayana Military Commander, Major-General Kiki Syahakri, the Chief of Police of East Nusa Tenggara, Brigadier-General E Made Mangku Pastika, representatives of the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and local government, as well as non-governmental organizations.
In Kupang, visited the regional police office to witness the destruction of a number of confiscated weapons.
In Kupang, visited the Noelbaki refugee camp.
In Atambua, the Mission visited the Haliwen refugee camp as well as the Umaklaran resettlement site.
In Atambua, held discussions with representatives of civil society and non-governmental organizations.
In Atambua, laid flowers at the UNHCR office, in honour of those killed on 6 September 2000, and were briefed on the events leading to the murders.

In Jakarta, met with Vice-President Megawati Sukarnoputri, and senior government officials, including the Coordinating Minister for Political, Social and Security Affairs, Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, the Speaker of the House of Representatives (DPR), Akbar Tandjung, Attorney-General Marzuki Darusman, and the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Alwi Shihab.
In Jakarta, met with representatives of the National Commission for Human Rights (Komnas HAM), the diplomatic community, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations.
A joint press conference was held in Jakarta on 17 November, at which Foreign Affairs Minister Shihab and the head of the Mission, Ambassador Andjaba, issued press statements.
In Kupang, some members of the Mission met with representatives from UNTAS (Uni Timor Aswain).
